data.article_summary: 《Sneakers》（1992）是一部关于一名安全专家和他的团队受命取回重要物品时，过去的秘密却回来困扰他们的电影。这部电影的蓝光版本在视频和音频质量上表现出色，视频和音频评分均为5.0，特别收录内容评分为3.5。蓝光版本采用MPEG-4 AVC编码，分辨率为4K (2160p)，配有DTS-HD Master Audio 5.1和2.0音轨，以及英文字幕。该蓝光碟为单碟BD-50，带有初版 slipcover 包装，区域编码为A区锁定。亚马逊售价为13.99美元，较原价24.95美元节省44%。目前用户评分7.3，音画质量广受好评。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电影《Sneakers》的技术细节、影响、重制质量以及相关文化 reference

不同观点：
• **对电影中密码学技术细节的赞赏**：
   - [psanford] 认为电影中的密码学技术细节（如数域筛法）非常准确，称赞了顾问的专业性。
   - [jackgavigan] 补充说，电影中的核心概念（如RSA加密）至今仍具有可信度，并提到自己受电影影响而对密码学产生兴趣，甚至影响了职业选择。他还提到RSA的共同发明人Leonard Adleman参与了电影中讲座场景的台词和幻灯片设计。

• **电影对个人和社会的影响**：
   - [meifun] 表示电影帮助他理解盲人学生的不同感知方式，并意识到社会工程学的存在和政府的秘密行为。
   - [jackgavigan] 也提到电影激发了他对密码学的兴趣，影响了他的职业道路。

• **对重制版本质量的批评和讨论**：
   - [xattt] 对一些老电影（如《Sneakers》和《辛普森一家》）在流媒体上的重制质量表示不满，指出明显的画质问题，质疑工作室是否对作品不够重视。
   - [BLKNSLVR] 则持不同观点，认为《Sneakers》更适合VHS质量的观看体验。

• **对电影的怀旧和喜爱**：
   - [Cyphase] 分享了个人对VHS录影带版本的怀旧记忆，并重温了电影中的经典场景和对白。
   - [pwrrr] 表示《Sneakers》是他最喜欢的黑客电影之一，并提到电影中的台词令人印象深刻。
   - [gittes] 称赞电影的演员阵容和导演，指出导演也执导了《梦幻成真》（Field of Dreams）。

• **对文化 reference 的讨论**：
   - [owlninja] 提到《Uncle Buck》也获得了重制，分享了一篇相关文章。
   - [int0x21] 提到在团队问答中使用“Setec Astronomy”作为队名但无人理解，感到遗憾。
   - [jph] 解释了“Setoc Astronomy”是电影中的一个密码学 reference，并表示这是他的最爱之一。

补充讨论：
• **对盗版和资源获取的讨论**：
   - [jack_pp] 提到对4K版本的资源获取速度感到惊讶，并指出私人种子比公开网站更早出现。

• **其他**：
   - [voxadam] 引用了电影中的经典台词“My voice is my passport. Verify Me.”，表达了对电影的喜爱和怀旧。

争议焦点：
• 电影重制版本的质量问题引发了对工作室是否对作品不够重视的争论。

data.title: Pixels in Islamic Art: Square Kufic Calligraphy (2020)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了伊斯兰书法中的平方库法体（Square Kufic），一种具有装饰性和复杂结构的艺术形式。平方库法体源自12至13世纪，可能起源于建筑中的阿拉伯文字适应。与传统库法体的严格规则不同，平方库法体允许字母变形以适应形状，有时会使文字难以辨认，增加了隐藏信息的趣味。尽管如此，保持填充和空白区域的均匀性是必须遵循的规则，有时也会故意留空以创造图案。平方库法体通常以重复和旋转的方式构成图案，具有像素化的特点，适合现代美学。文章还提到了两位现代平方库法体艺术家：Kamal Boullata和Ahmed Moustafa。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对Kufi脚本及其相关艺术风格的讨论和联想

不同观点：
• otras: 欣赏Jeff Erickson算法书封面上的al-Khwarizmi风格，并提供了相关链接以供参考。

• omneity: 指出Kufi书写起源于伊拉克库法地区，并提到库法地区也是Kufiyyeh头巾的发源地，提供了维基百科链接。
• samirillian: 澄清第一张图片并非Kufic脚本，并质疑关于只有两种书写风格的说法，认为还有更多种类的脚本。
• sudahtigabulan: 认为一个提供的图片不是Kufic脚本，但分享了自己最喜欢的一个例子。
• hnlmorg: 提到维基百科上有一些不错的Kufic脚本例子，并联想到伦敦地铁迷宫图案。

43899251.article_content:
When I was a little kid whenever we drove by mosques, I would be intrigued by the complex motifs they’re decorated by. I always tried to figure out the pattern; to me it was just a pattern, I never thought it can be writing because they didn’t look like letters from any alphabet I knew at the time. I remember thinking that I had finally found a full pattern that was only to be broken in the next square. As I grew older I learned that these pieces that resemble a labyrinth, at first sight, have so much more to offer than just lush visuals. Verses from the Quran were taken and turned into striking artwork carrying valuable messages. The more I learned about Islamic calligraphy and especially square Kufic, the more interesting it became and I will be delighted to share this fascination with my readers.
The importance of calligraphy in Islamic culture is indisputable. Unlike in Christian culture, the visual depiction of verses from the Holy Book is not used in decoration. Calligraphy shows itself reciting the Quran with beautiful writing decorating everything from mosques to plates to clothes to carpets. Islamic Calligraphy derives from two main styles; Naskh and Kufic. The peculiarity of Kufic Calligraphy is the straight and structured lettering. The Kufic style in itself comes in a variety of styles such as floriated, square, knotted, new style…  The patterns that appear complex and random comes with strict rules and systematics. This form of Islamic Art is gaining popularity again due to its moderln and graphic look and resurfacing the traditional alluring patterns.
Work done by Sergio Fabris found on
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kufic_mjriam_nach_Fabris.jpg
(no changes were made)              This image is licensed under the
Creative Commons
Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International
license.
Square Kufic dates all the way back to the 12th-13th century. Sometimes it is also referred to as banna-i which is a Farsi word and it is mostly used to refer to the architectural square Kufic. There are two main theories about how Square Kufic came into being. The first one suggests a fusion between the Arabic script and the Chinese seal script; the Arabic script was fitted into the forms of Chinese scripts and created square Kufic. The second theory argues that it came from architectural adaptations of Arabic script. The second theory seems to be more accreditable and I saw some articles mentioning this assumption as well. This is further supported by the first examples of square Kufic. These were seen in architecture and was done using bricks packed next to one another. The earliest example is from Ghazni (modern-day Afghanistan) in Sultan Meshud Tower also known as the Victory Towers or Masud III Tower.
Shada written in square Kufic style, shaped like buildings
As I have mentioned above, Kufic calligraphy has strict rules but in square Kufic, these rules are often bent, and even broken. The letters and the overall script is skewed to fit it into shape. This is why sometimes it can be very hard to decipher what was written in the text. I think the fact that it is not always done to pass on the message openly excites me too. Having a somewhat hidden message in the image makes things a lot more amusing. The only rule that is always followed is keeping the filled out and empty spaces even especially when it comes to thickess. Although this is the rule, the artist might knowingly leave out spaces to create a pattern within the pattern. Typically, the diacritical dots are not used when writing down the script in this form but there are examples of square Kufic using diacritical dots as well. Sometimes dots are used not for diacritical purposes but as filler dots.
The technicalities can get a little bit confusing but I’ll do my best to simplify them and keep it short. The script is written commonly clockwise but it can be anticlockwise or a zigzag pattern. Furthermore, the direction of the writing can change midway to make it fit into the shape. Not only the direction of writing but even the letters and their forms are played with to fill up space evenly. Although the name is Square Kufic, there are many shapes the script can be fitted into. Most commonly it is rectangular shapes but it can be even other words that the Kufic is written into. Once a verse or a single word is written in Square Kufic form, it can be repeated to create a pattern. Sometimes the initial piece is rotated in various ways to create different patterns. This is why I think it is sort of like a pixel, it is the one of many which an image, pattern is created. I envisage that the flexibility it has in comparison to other forms of Kufic makes it easier to adapt to the aesthetic likes we have today. There are two modern-day square Kufic artists that I very much enjoy the work of. These are Kamal Boullata and Ahmed Moustafa. data.title: VMOS – Virtual Android on Android
data.author: danboarder
data.article_summary: VMOS Pro是一款能够在安卓设备上运行虚拟安卓系统的应用，具备独立系统，支持小内存设备，并允许用户在同一设备上同时运行两个社交账户，适用于生活和工作分离。它提供ROOT环境，支持多种ROOT游戏，并具备画中画模式和后台运行功能，不影响前台操作。用户可自定义分辨率，设置高度、宽度和DPI。要求手机存储不低于32GB，RAM不低于2GB，系统版本需为安卓5.1或更高。已订阅Google Play上VMOS Premium的用户可在VMOS Pro中享受同等特权。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VMOS Pro Android 5.1 ROM的版权声明及其使用价值

不同观点：
• [eniac111] 引用了VMOS Pro Android 5.1 ROM的GitHub README中的版权声明，强调未经授权的使用将受到法律追究，并提到举报侵权行为有奖励。该评论关注版权保护和法律行动。
• [ashirviskas] 对声明中的标点符号和语法错误表示不信任，质疑其合法性和专业性。
• [gitroom] 认为版权警告没有实际意义，并质疑使用VMOS的必要性，指出Android系统本身已经具备许多账户分离的功能。
• [outadoc] 进一步支持gitroom的观点，指出Android的工作资料和用户账户功能已经可以实现VMOS所声称的功能，质疑其作为卖点的说服力。
• [voidUpdate] 关注网站的设计和用户体验问题，如字体样式和滚动效果，与版权声明无直接关系。
• [jemzipx] 将VMOS与Samsung Knox进行比较，询问其优劣，可能在考虑其他类似功能的产品。
• [ac_15] 直接质疑为何不使用Android系统自带的配置文件功能，暗示VMOS可能没有存在的必要。
• [RockRobotRock] 发表了一句简短且模糊的批评，没有提供具体论据。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是VMOS Pro Android 5.1 ROM的版权声明及其法律效力，部分用户对其合法性和执行力表示怀疑。
• 另一个讨论要点是VMOS的功能价值，多位用户指出Android系统已经具备类似的多账户管理功能，质疑VMOS的必要性和竞争力。
• 此外，还有用户关注网站的设计和用户体验问题，虽然这些与主要讨论点无直接关系，但反映了用户对整体体验的关注。

总的来说，讨论围绕VMOS的版权声明及其功能价值展开，部分用户对其必要性和合法性提出质疑。

data.title: Carolina Eyck, renowned superstar of the theremin
data.author: asdefghyk
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了被誉为最杰出的特雷门琴演奏家卡罗莱娜·艾克（Carolina Eyck）的经历与贡献。特雷门琴是一种无需接触的独特乐器，通过操控电磁场发声，常被用来营造诡异的音效。艾克在七岁时开始学习这种乐器，并在16岁时革新了演奏方法，后来撰写了《特雷门琴演奏艺术》一书，成为该乐器的权威指南。她指出，演奏特雷门琴需要与乐器和身体的高度协调，创造了一种自由与控制的平衡。艾克还提到，特雷门琴让她在音乐表达和社会联系上感受到了自由。文章最后提到她将在与澳大利亚室内乐团巡演中首演新作《气垫船》。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Theremin乐器的使用、历史、技术特点以及其在音乐和文化中的影响

不同观点：
• **对Theremin音色的评价**：
   - [perilunar] 认为Theremin的声音听起来不愉快，尽管它是一个完全电子的乐器，理论上可以发出任何声音。
   - [dewster] 提到他设计的开源D-Lev数字Theremin，展示了现代技术对该乐器的改进。

• **Theremin的演奏者与演奏技巧**：
   - [davidw] 提到Fishbone乐队的Angelo Moore偶尔使用Theremin，但并不如他演奏其他乐器时那样出色。
   - [pdpi] 提到YouTuber Rob Scallon与Carolina合作的一个视频，详细介绍了如何演奏Theremin，对于感兴趣的人来说是一个不错的资源。

• **Theremin的历史与技术背景**：
   - [alexjplant] 指出"Good Vibrations"这首歌实际上是用Electro-Theremin录制的，并解释了Electro-Theremin与传统Theremin的区别。同时提到Ondes Martenot这种乐器与Theremin的区别。
   - [srean] 提到了"The Thing"这个基于Theremin原理的窃听装置，强调了其历史和技术背景。

• **Theremin的现代应用与购买建议**：
   - [fxj] 提到目前仍有公司生产Theremin，如Doepfer和Stylophone，并提供了相关产品链接和演示视频。
   - [calamity_elf] 分享了自己在1980年代自制Theremin的经历，并表示现在考虑购买一个现代的Theremin。

• **Theremin在音乐和文化中的特殊应用**：
   - [totikom] 提到Theremin被用于录制向地外文明传递的信息"Teen Age Message"。
   - [opminion] 提到了一次针对家庭观众的Theremin表演，认为由于过度简化和冗长的解释，表演效果打了折扣。

• **Theremin的个人体验与感受**：
   - [BrtByte] 强调了Theremin的个人化特点，认为它将演奏者与乐器融为一体，具有神秘感。
   - [cess11] 对一位Theremin演奏者的表演给予高度评价，并提供了她演奏Ennio Morricone作品的视频链接。

补充讨论：
• **对Theremin的幽默与对比**：
   - [lars512] 以幽默的方式提到自己以为会讨论一种更复杂的乐器。
   - [epizootics] 分享了一个向Lèon Theremin致敬的视频链接。

争议焦点：
• **Theremin音色的争议**：部分人对其音色持负面评价，认为其声音不如其他乐器悦耳，而其他人则对其神秘感和个人化特点表示赞赏。

总结：评论主要围绕Theremin的音色、演奏技巧、历史背景及其在现代和文化中的应用展开，展现了对该乐器的不同看法和体验。

Uncanny, spooky, weird. The theremin is a musical instrument with baggage. Depending on your vintage, it’s the aliens landing in
The Day The Earth Stood Still
or the haunting waltz of
Midsomer Murders
. It’s the whiplash shriek in the crazy breakdown of
Whole Lotta Love,
Miss Huang’s instrument of choice during the camping trip in
Severance
or the trippy wobble in
Good Vibrations
. The fact that that last example isn’t actually theremin but a soundalike synthesiser only illustrates how entrenched the high-pitched, wide-vibrato, “woo-ooo” sound has become as a signifier of weirdness: a go-to vibe for the modern composer’s quantum leap to Far Out.
None of this applied, mind you, to seven-year-old Carolina Eyck, studying classical violin and piano in East Germany in the ’90s. The theremin in the loungeroom was just another gizmo Dad acquired for his synth band, shelved on the grounds of difficulty. “You need to practise,” she says with impish understatement.
With its sci-fi antennae bristling left and right, Russian physicist Leon Theremin’s novel invention of 1919 remains the only musical instrument you play without touching anything. “Aerial fingering” was the technique devised by the inventor’s original Lithuanian prodigy, Clara Rockmore, in the 1930s.
Leon Theremin with his groundbreaking hands-off instrument.
At the age of 16, Eyck revolutionised that method and in her 20s, she literally wrote the modern manual:
The Art of Playing the Theremin
. Today, widely considered the instrument’s most accomplished virtuoso, she’s practised in explaining its mysteries.
“I came up with the eight finger positions,” she says, snapping shapes at shoulder height with her right hand. “A closed hand is a basic note, and then open hand is the octave …” She plays the scale as if making shadow puppets in thin air.
“In my new book that I’m releasing, hopefully soon, I expanded the whole system into 40 positions. It sounds a lot,” she says with a laugh, “but it just makes so much sense.”
Advertisement
Eyck agrees that the sight of a human body manipulating invisible electromagnetic fields adds to the theremin’s otherworldly aura. The fact that it sounds like nothing so much as an unhinged soprano – listen again to the original
Star Trek
theme – adds to the unsettling effect.
“You don’t tune it to the A from the piano, but you tune it to your own body and to the surroundings,” she says, citing something called “body capacitance”. In this way the instrument is unique, “except for the voice, but that’s inside you”.
Carolina Eyck is performing as part of the Theremin & Beyond tour.
Credit:
Ananda Costa
“With the theremin, you are a part of the instrument because you’re within the electromagnetic fields. I like to [say] that the theremin consists of four different parts: the theremin itself … then the electromagnetic fields … then you need a loudspeaker to create a sound, and the fourth part is your body; the player that plays it.”
Loading
Eyck has heard the theory that the instrument is somehow more attuned to female energies. She was taught by Leon Theremin’s grand-niece Lydia Kavina. Notable contemporaries include Austrian sound artist Dorit Chrysler and Iceland’s Hekla Magnúsdóttir.
“There is something sensual to it,” she says, “but there are wonderful male players as well. Like with dance or, really, any musical instrument, you just need a sense of your own body and
feeling
the music.”
Advertisement
In one of her many educational videos online, she comes close to invoking a spiritual dimension to her practice. The meditative stillness required to command the space amounts to “being in harmony with yourself … It has helped me to become free,” she says.
“On the mental level ... when you study classical music … you have to go through exams; you are constantly judged. You can [get] very nervous on stage,” she says. “With the theremin, I always experienced that I wasn’t part of that. I had my own system. I can invent my own technique. And when I’m on stage, nobody knows what I’m doing … That gave me a lot of freedom mentally.
Eyck says there is something sensual about the theremin.
Credit:
Shai Levy
“Also socially, to connect with people around the world, because there were so few of us. I could go to England, and I would meet friends that I’ve never met because of that. And then also, while playing, I feel sort of free. Of course I need to hit the notes, but you are in space, and the balance between control and freedom is there. So those three aspects, for me, gave me freedom.”
Airborne liberty and retro-futuristic novelty are both playfully invoked in
Hovercraft
, a new commission by Sydney composer Holly Harrison which will make its world premiere on Eyck’s tour with Richard Tognetti and the Australian Cha

data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Anukari 3D Physics Synthesizer在Apple Silicon macOS设备上的性能问题及其解决方案请求。Anukari是一个实时音频生成工具，依赖GPU进行大规模物理模拟。由于macOS的电源管理机制，当GPU负载较低时，系统会降低其时钟频率，导致Anukari无法满足实时音频处理的低延迟需求。作者通过Apple的Metal profiler发现问题在于GPU的时钟频率，并在当前解决方案中通过一个辅助工作负载“欺骗”系统以提高GPU时钟频率，使Anukari在大多数设备上运行良好。然而，为了在所有Apple设备上实现可靠性能，作者希望与Apple Metal团队直接沟通，以解决这一技术问题。

43901619.article_content:
devlog
An Appeal to Apple from Anukari
TL;DR: To make Anukari’s performance reliable across all Apple silicon macOS devices, I need to talk to someone on the Apple Metal team. It would be great if someone can connect me with the right person inside Apple, or direct them to my feedback request FB17475838 as well as this devlog entry.
This is going to be a VERY LONG HIGHLY TECHNICAL post, so either buckle your seatbelt or leave while you still can.
Background
The
Anukari 3D Physics Synthesizer
simulates a large spring-mass model in real-time for audio generation. To support a nontrivial number of physics objects, it requires a GPU for the simulation. The physics code is ALU-bound, not memory-bound. All mutable state in the simulation is stored in the GPU’s threadgroup memory, which is roughly equivalent to a manually-allocated L1 cache, so it is extremely fast.
The typical use-case for Anukari is running it as an AudioUnit (AU) or VST3 plugin inside a host application like Pro Tools or Ableton, also called a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW). The DAW invokes Anukari for each audio buffer block, which is a request to generate/process N samples of audio. For each block, Anukari invokes the physics simulation GPU kernel, waits for the result, and returns.
The audio buffer block system is important because GPU kernel scheduling has a certain amount of latency overhead, and for real-time audio we have fixed time constraints. By amortizing the GPU scheduling latency over, say, 512 audio samples, it becomes negligible. But the runtime of the kernel itself is still very important.
Basic Problem
Apple’s macOS is obviously extremely clever about power management, and Apple silicon hardware is built to support the OS in achieving high power efficiency.
As with all modern hardware, the clock rate for Apple silicon chips can be slowed down to reduce power consumption. When the OS detects that the processing demand for a given chip is low (or non-existent), it can decrease the clock rate for that chip. This is awesome.
The problem is that due to the way Anukari runs inside a DAW and interacts with the GPU, the heuristics that macOS uses to determine whether there is sufficient demand upon the GPU to increase its clock rate do not work.
Consider the chart below. The CPU does some preparatory work, there’s a small gap which represents kernel invocation latency, and then the GPU does a large block of work. Finally there’s another small gap representing the real-time headroom.
(An aside: chalkboards are way better than whiteboards, unless you enjoy getting high on noxious fumes. in which case whiteboards are the way to go.)
I don’t have any real knowledge of macOS’s heuristics for deciding when to increase the GPU clock speed, but I might reasonably guess that it relies on something like the
load average
. In the diagram above, the GPU load average might be only 60%, because between audio buffer blocks it is idle. Perhaps this does not meet the threshold for increasing the GPU clock rate.
But this is terrible for Anukari, because to meet real-time constraints, it needs the absolute lowest latency possible, which requires the highest GPU clock rate. I’m not sure how low the Apple GPU clock rate can go, but it definitely goes low enough to make Anukari unusable.
To be clear, it’s pretty understandable that macOS handles this situation poorly, because the GPU is mostly used for throughput workflows like graphics or ML. Audio on the GPU is really new, and there are only a couple of companies doing it right now.
Are you sure the clock rate is the problem?
Oh yes.
Thankfully, Apple’s first-part Instruments tools that come with Xcode have a handy Metal profiler. Among other things, this is how I first learned that Anukari is ALU-bound.
The Metal profiler has an incredibly useful feature: it allows you to choose the Metal “Performance State” while profiling the application. This is not configurable outside of the profiler. This is how I first figured out that the GPU clock rate was the issue: Anukari works perfectly under the Maximum performance state, and abysmally under the Minimum performance state.
Wait, Anukari mostly works great on macOS. How is that possible?
Given the explanation above, this is a great question. Most people with macOS find that Anukari works great. For example, I intentionally bought a base-model Macbook M1 for development, so that if Anukari worked well for me, I’d know it worked well for people with beefier hardware.
So how is it that Anukari works great on macOS for most people? Well, as Steve Jobs said, “It’s better to be a pirate than to join the Navy.”
Without being able to rely on macOS to do the right thing, I thought like a pirate and came up with a workaround: in parallel with the audio computation on the GPU, Anukari runs a second workload on the GPU that is designed to create a high load average and trick macOS into clocking up the GPU. This workload is tuned to use as little of the GPU as possible,

data.title: An Interactive Debugger for Rust Trait Errors
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为Argus的交互式调试工具，用于帮助Rust开发者理解复杂的trait错误。Rust的类型系统能够有效捕获简单错误，但对于涉及trait的复杂错误，编译器生成的错误信息往往难以理解。尤其是使用Diesel等ORM库时，错误信息可能包含大量细节，增加了开发者调试的难度。Argus通过图形界面（GUI）让开发者逐步探索trait求解器的推理树，提供直观的错误诊断方式，支持展开简略信息、查看完整路径和实现细节等功能。用户研究表明，这种交互式界面能够有效帮助开发者理解和解决trait相关错误。Argus可作为VSCode插件使用，其源代码已在GitHub上开放。

不同观点：

• quotemstr对Rust的错误提示受到赞誉表示质疑，指出过去C++的元编程错误调试也曾受到批评，认为Rust的类似功能不应被视为优越之处，并提到了Templight项目作为例子。

43901985.article_content:
An Interactive Debugger for Rust Trait Errors
Gavin Gray
·
April 29, 2025
Human developers frequently make simple mistakes. Thankfully, type systems do a great job of statically catching simple mistakes and saving developers time. However, as type errors become more complex, developers may spend significant time trying to understand the error message itself.
Imagine writing a social media platform in Rust. Say your application has two tables,
users
and
posts
, the latter has a field
author_id
that is a foreign key into the users table. You want to write a function that fetches all users and their published posts from the database; typing hastily — or accepting code from Copilot — you end up with the following buggy function. (The full code is available
here
.)
fn
get_all_published_posts
(
conn
:
&mut
PgConnection
)
->
QueryResult
<
Vec
<(
i32
,
String
,
i32
)>> {
users
::
table
.
filter
(
posts
::
published
.
eq
(
true
))
.
select
((
users
::
id
,
users
::
name
,
posts
::
id
))
.
load
(
conn
)
}
A Rust function that uses the Diesel library to select columns from a
SQL
table.
For anyone familiar with
SQL
, the error should be easy to spot. You've forgotten to join the users and posts tables! Although that error is easy to describe in English, it's tricky for the compiler. The >100 line, 650 word, 7.6k character error message below is the information you'd get back from the Rust compiler. (The raw text is also available
here
.)
Expand
error[E0277]: Cannot select `posts::columns::id` from `users::table`
--> src/main.rs:30:10
|
30 |         .select((users::id, users::name, posts::id))
|          ^^^^^^ the trait `SelectableExpression<users::table>` is not implemented for `posts::columns::id`
|
= note: `posts::columns::id` is no valid selection for `users::table`
= help: the following other types implement trait `SelectableExpression<QS>`:
`posts::columns::id` implements `SelectableExpression<JoinOn<Join, On>>`
`posts::columns::id` implements `SelectableExpression<Only<posts::table>>`
`posts::columns::id` implements `SelectableExpression<SelectStatement<FromClause<From>>>`
`posts::columns::id` implements `SelectableExpression<Tablesample<posts::table, TSM>>`
`posts::columns::id` implements `SelectableExpression<posts::table>`
`posts::columns::id` implements `SelectableExpression<query_source::joins::Join<Left, Right, Inner>>`
`posts::columns::id` implements `SelectableExpression<query_source::joins::Join<Left, Right, LeftOuter>>`
The error message from the Rust compiler for the Diesel program above.
The issue is that Diesel, the Rust
ORM
library being used, contains a complex system of
traits
to check domain-specific correctness properties, like the validity of
SQL
queries. Even for a language with famously good error messages like Rust, explaining why these traits fail is a tall order.
I know what you, the reader, are thinking:
I use better languages and this seems like a Rust problem.
Unfortunately, it isn't just a Rust problem. Many languages have type features similar to Rust's traits (Haskell
type classes,
Scala
givens,
Swift
protocols,
C++
concepts,
etc). Moreover, it's not even a problem with just traits, it's a general problem with complex type mechanisms. For example, a Rust trait error is discovered by the trait solver, a component that is a black box to Rust developers. Rust diagnostics use information from the solver's internal data structure, the trait inference tree, to generate diagnostics. As the complexity of type systems increase, so does the size and complexity of the compiler's black-box innards, which places a greater burden on the compiler to explain itself. Today, this is a Herculean task for modern languages.
In response, we developed Argus, an interactive trait debugger for Rust. Argus provides an interface into the full inference tree generated by the trait solver. Argus uses a
GUI
rather than a
CLI
, allowing the developer to incrementally explore the complexity of the inference tree. Here is a live demo of Argus running on the Diesel program above:
Loading...
An Argus widget for the Diesel error discussed above. Try clicking around!
Argus presents two views on the inference tree: bottom-up (starting from the leaves) and top-down (starting from the root). Notice that most of the content of the message is tucked behind various interactions:
The rest of the inference tree can be accessed by clicking the individual trait bounds.
Long types and impl bounds have been abbreviated with a
[..]
which can be expanded by clicking.
Paths have been abbreviated, and full paths can be seen by mousing over the path (sorry touchscreen readers).
A list of implementations of a trait can be accessed by clicking the list icon to the right of each trait bound.
You can try Argus as a VSCode extension on the
VSCode Marketplace
or the
Open VSX Registry
. The Argus source code is available on
Github
.
In addition, we ran a user study to test our hypothesis that our interactive interface is useful to developers.
43901985.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为Argus的交互式调试工具，用于帮助Rust开发者理解复杂的trait错误。Rust的类型系统能够有效捕获简单错误，但对于涉及trait的复杂错误，编译器生成的错误信息往往难以理解。尤其是使用Diesel等ORM库时，错误信息可能包含大量细节，增加了开发者调试的难度。Argus通过图形界面（GUI）让开发者逐步探索trait求解器的推理树，提供直观的错误诊断方式，支持展开简略信息、查看完整路径和实现细节等功能。用户研究表明，这种交互式界面能够有效帮助开发者理解和解决trait相关错误。Argus可作为VSCode插件使用，其源代码已在GitHub上开放。

主要讨论点：不同编程语言的编译错误提示和调试难度比较

不同观点：
• Rygian认为例子中的问题已经通过错误提示清晰展现，特别是错误信息指出了在查询中遗漏了`posts`表，并认为这些提示足够帮助定位问题。他还表示多余的帮助信息可以忽略不计。

• KingOfCoders提到在Scala编程中，长类型错误信息曾经很难处理，并表示Rust编译器的错误提示是他目前最喜欢的，认为其对开发者生产力有帮助，提供了一个链接作为参考。

• Meneth认为Zig语言的编译时调用堆栈可能比Rust的Trait错误提示提供更好的错误报告，暗示Zig在错误报告方面可能优于Rust。

• quotemstr对Rust的错误提示受到赞誉表示质疑，指出过去C++的元编程错误调试也曾受到批评，认为Rust的类似功能不应被视为优越之处，并提到了Templight项目作为例子。

data.author: vitto_gioda

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Skype的兴衰、其替代品以及与微软Teams的关系

不同观点：
• **Skype的历史与技术问题**：
  - colmmacc回顾了2007年Skype大规模宕机事件，指出其技术架构中的超级节点问题，并提到尽管出现多日全球性宕机，Skype依然成功多次出售，表明其业务的恢复力和韧性。
  
• **Skype的衰落与Zoom、Discord等替代品的崛起**：
  - OliveMate认为Skype从2010年的领先地位迅速衰落，到2020年几乎无人问津，尤其是在疫情期间，Zoom和Discord等竞争对手迅速崛起，而微软的Teams未能及时填补市场需求。
  - sillystu04指出Skype本有机会成为WhatsApp、Zoom或Discord，但在多个领域都未能把握机会。

• **Skype功能的消失与用户体验的变化**：
  - guiriduro和flynumber提到Skype的DID服务和与电话网络的整合功能消失，导致用户不得不转向SIP客户端，批评微软对Skype的调整不当。
  - tim333抱怨Skype关闭时未退还用户账户中的余额，认为这种做法不公平。

• **Skype替代品的讨论**：
  - 多位用户（loloquwowndueo, flynumber, billpg）在寻找替代Skype进行国际电话呼叫的方案，提出了Viber、Rebtel等应用，但表示仍在寻找更好的选择。

• **Teams与Skype的品牌和功能比较**：
  - internet_points和bluenose69等用户对Teams取代Skype表示不满，指出Teams更多地面向企业而非个人用户，认为Teams在用户体验上不如Skype，并抱怨其复杂性和强制使用。
  - andyjohnson0认为Teams的免费版本在个人通讯市场中的品牌定位不佳，猜测多数用户已转向WhatsApp。

补充讨论：
• **用户对Skype关闭的情感反应**：
  - donohoe提到其组织为Skype的退出举行了告别仪式，表达了对Skype的情感，但承认更多是怀念其理念而非实际使用。

• **技术兼容性问题**：
  - Aardwolf担心Teams无法像Skype一样在Linux浏览器中使用，对Teams的技术兼容性提出疑问。

争议焦点：
• Skype在疫情期间被Zoom等应用取代的原因，以及微软在Skype向Teams过渡中的不当处理。
• Teams作为Skype继承者的定位是否合理，尤其是在个人通讯市场中的表现和用户体验。

data.title: DoorDash to acquire Deliveroo
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 英国外卖公司Deliveroo同意了美国竞争对手DoorDash的收购提案，DoorDash将以每股180便士的价格收购Deliveroo全部已发行和将发行股票，交易对Deliveroo的估值为29亿英镑。这一价格较4月4日收盘价溢价44%。Deliveroo股价随后升至三年高点。DoorDash CEO表示，合并后将覆盖40多个国家、超10亿人口，助力本地企业发展。此次收购标志着Deliveroo动荡的上市公司生涯结束，其股价自2021年IPO以来已下跌超过50%。对DoorDash而言，收购Deliveroo是其海外扩展的重要一步，此前它已在2022年收购了芬兰外卖应用Wolt。食品外卖行业近年来持续整合，竞争激烈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：外卖配送服务的优缺点、市场竞争与创新潜力

不同观点：
• **质疑外卖配送服务的价值**：[prmoustache] 认为人们因为懒惰而使用配送服务，但付额外费用、等待更长时间、收到冷饭菜是不值得的。除非配送服务能从较远的地方送餐并保持食物温度，否则没有吸引力。目前只有披萨店相对做得好，因为它们有自己的配送服务。

• **推崇传统用餐模式**：[gregorvand] 认为像新加坡的小贩中心那样，出门步行十分钟内可以享受廉价美食，无需配送费用和制造额外排放，还能与他人交流，这种模式更好。

• **经济角度分析**：[FlyingSnake] 分享了一篇关于外卖应用程序经济学的文章，指出其中的经济操作如“披萨套利”。

• **对现有服务不满**：[Havoc] 表示如果不是因为有美国运通的折扣，根本不会使用Deliveroo，暗示对服务的不满。

• **对小费文化的担忧**：[Raed667] 预测DoorDash会使小费变得更烦人和侵入性，期待看欧洲用户的反应。

• **配送员问题**：[voidUpdate] 抱怨每次外卖员都找不到他的公寓，尽管他已经很清晰地标注了位置，质疑配送员的导航能力。

• **品牌名称讨论**：[modeless] 认为Deliveroo这个品牌名更好听。

• **市场竞争与并购**：[morpheuskafka] 提到Deliveroo的香港业务卖给了Foodpanda，DoorDash只对某些市场感兴趣。

• **垄断与资本主义批评**：[Frieren] 认为这些并购旨在减少竞争和创造垄断，批评资本主义环境下的这种行为。

• **欧洲市场担忧**：[Argonaut998] 对欧洲公司被美国公司收购表示担忧，质疑这些交易为何被批准。

• **功能需求**：[ksynwa] 希望这些应用程序能允许外卖自取。

• **国际市场扩展**：[omneity] 询问DoorDash是否在进入新市场。

• **创新缺失与未来展望**：[gorgoiler] 认为Deliveroo错失了在应用程序中加入社交元素和创新的机会，目前只是扩展了配送范围，缺乏对消费者和配送员的长期价值。期待有新的服务能专注于餐厅、食物质量和服务的提升。

补充讨论：
• 对英国创业环境的不满：[colesantiago] 指出英国的初创公司大多数要么被外国买家收购，要么关闭或迁往美国，反映了英国市场的困境。

这些观点揭示了用户对于外卖配送服务的多角度看法，包括服务质量、经济效益、市场竞争和创新潜力等方面。争议焦点主要在于服务费用与体验的不匹配以及对垄断趋势的担忧。

Key Points
British food delivery firm Deliveroo said its board agreed to an offer from DoorDash to acquire all issued and to be issued shares in the company for 180 pence a share.
That marks a 44% premium to Deliveroo's closing price on April 4, the last business day prior to DoorDash's initial offer letter.
The transaction values Deliveroo at £2.9 billion on a fully diluted basis.
In this article

CREATE FREE ACCOUNT
A Deliveroo rider near Victoria station in London, England, on March 31, 2021.
Dan Kitwood | Getty Images
LONDON — British food delivery firm
Deliveroo
on Tuesday said it has agreed to a takeover offer from American rival DoorDash that values the company at £2.9 billion ($3.9 billion).
Deliveroo, which lets users order hot meals and groceries via an app, said its board agreed to an offer from DoorDash to acquire all issued and to be issued shares in the company for 180 pence a share.
That marks a 44% premium to Deliveroo's closing price on April 4, the last business day prior to DoorDash's initial offer letter.
Deliveroo shares jumped to a
three-year high
last week after the company confirmed it had received a takeover offer from DoorDash.
The transaction values Deliveroo at £2.9 billion on a fully diluted basis, the company said.
DoorDash said that the financial terms of the acquisition were final and would not be increased unless a third party steps in with a rival bid.
"I could not be more excited by the prospect of what DoorDash and Deliveroo will be able to accomplish together. We'll cover more than 40 countries with a combined population of more than 1 billion people, enabling us to provide more local businesses with the tools and technology they need to thrive," said Tony Xu, CEO and Co-founder of DoorDash.
International expansion
The acquisition deal marks an end to Deliveroo's tumultuous ride as a public company.
Once viewed as a British tech darling, Deliveroo saw its shares tank 30% in 2021 in one of the worst trading debuts on the London Stock Exchange. Shares have continued to fall from that point and are down more than 50% from the firm's £3.90 IPO price.
Get a weekly round up of the top tech stories from around the world in your inbox every Friday.
Subscribe
Deliveroo went public at a time when the U.K. was still feeling the impacts of Covid-19 lockdowns, which had boosted the fortunes of various food delivery platforms. Investors questioned the sustainability of that growth in a post-Covid world, and saw intense competition in the market and legal challenges to the gig economy model as key risks for Deliveroo.
For DoorDash, acquiring Deliveroo marks a renewed effort from the American online takeout app to expand its presence overseas. DoorDash acquired Finnish food delivery app Wolt for 7 billion euros ($7.9 billion) in 2022.
More broadly, the food delivery sector has been undergoing consolidation for several years now. Earlier this year, Deliveroo
sold parts
of its Hong Kong unit to Delivery Hero, while
Just East
agreed to be acquired
by investment group Prosus.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AliExpress平台上的商品运输问题及其受到关税和物流限制的影响

不同观点：
• [wkat4242] 认为AliExpress本身并不直接发货，大部分卖家是自己发货，因此发货情况会因不同卖家而异。AliExpress只是一个交易平台，不能一概而论。
  
• [byoung2] 指出有供应商告知由于关税问题未解决，货物仍滞留在中国，暗示关税问题直接影响了商品的运输和交付。

• [pogue] 提到来自香港的货物被香港政府封锁，且DHL拒绝运输，这表明运输问题不仅源于关税，还涉及物流公司和地方政府的政策限制。

data.author: nill0

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Curry-Howard correspondence及其在编程和证明书写中的应用和教学价值

不同观点：
• elikoga认为，将"Propositions as Types"（命题即类型）/ Curry-Howard correspondence应用于教学中，可以帮助学生更好地掌握结构化的证明书写技巧，尤其是在函数式编程教学中。他认为这种方法能够帮助学生更好地处理证明中的蕴涵和量化问题。
• devlovstad从个人经验出发，表示虽然选修的语义与类型课程（涉及Curry-Howard correspondence的概念）对他有很大帮助，特别是在精确书写证明和理解程序执行方面，但这种课程在计算机科学学生中并不受欢迎，尤其是在人工智能热门的情况下。他还提到了一次对Phil Wadler演讲的失望经历。
• indyjo认为Curry-Howard correspondence被过度宣传为对程序员有用，但实际上它的应用范围有限，尤其是在主流编程语言中。他指出，虽然该理论在纯函数式编程语言中有用，但在命令式、状态化、并发等更常见的编程范式中应用难度大。他希望有更多努力将强大的形式化方法引入主流编程语言或开发更实用的编程语言。
• marcusb提供了另一个相关演讲的链接，供进一步了解Curry-Howard correspondence。
• js8推荐了一本关于Curry-Howard correspondence的书，强调了其在逻辑和类型关系方面的解释。
• gitroom表示，虽然在代码中进行正式证明能帮助捕捉错误，但实际操作中往往比直接修复问题更慢。
• aatd86建议进一步探讨集合论及其对类型的解释，以丰富对Curry-Howard correspondence的理解。
• emorning3表示不愿意手动证明代码正确性，而是希望通过逻辑规范自动生成代码，并询问是否有类似Prolog的工具。
• immibis认为Curry-Howard correspondence虽然有趣，但在实际编程中并不特别有用。他指出，很多对应命题的类型和程序并不能带来实际编程中的洞见，类似于将逻辑表达式转换为集合运算，只是符号不同，并无实质性新见解。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Curry-Howard correspondence在教育中的潜在价值的不同看法，有些人认为它对学生有帮助，而另一些人则认为它的实际应用有限。
• 对主流编程语言中引入形式化方法的期望和挑战也被提及，特别是在实用性和接受度方面。
• 一些参与者分享了个人学习经验和对相关资源的推荐，提供了进一步了解该主题的途径。
• 争议的焦点在于Curry-Howard correspondence的实际应用价值，尤其是在编程实践中的效用。

data.title: Getting things “done” in large tech companies
data.author: swah
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在大公司中“完成任务”的真正含义。与解决数学问题不同，现实世界中的任务，如种树或开发大型应用程序，永远有改进空间。对于技术公司的工程师来说，陷入无限小改进的陷阱会导致他们忽略真正的工作目标：为公司带来最大价值。要真正“完成任务”，需要做到两点：一是让公司决策者满意并理解你的工作成果，二是确保你的工作对上级可见且有意义。工程师应避免过度优化，而是在适当时宣布胜利并转向新任务。本文强调，“完成任务”是一种社会构建，尽管不完美，但它直接影响职业发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工程师在大公司中如何有效地完成工作并体现价值，以及在技术工作与管理层需求之间的平衡问题。

不同观点：
• **whstl**：认为工程师的工作变得过于专门化，与决策者和客户的需求脱节。Product Managers在工程师与公司其他部门之间造成了隔阂，使得工程师很难直接体现自己的价值。唯一让他感到满意的工作经历是在担任临时产品经理时，因为能直接与利益相关者沟通并了解他们的需求。

• **wpietri**：反对仅仅为了取悦权力高层而工作的观念。认为技术职业的终极目标不应只是让老板满意，而应关注更根本的技术成就，如解决实际问题或让工具正常运行。

• **d_burfoot**：指出工程师不仅要写代码，还需要做“销售”工作，如推广自己的工作、与客户沟通、理解业务等。在大公司中，工程师很难只专注于技术工作，而必须参与更多的跨部门协作和沟通。

• **al_borland**：批评了项目完成后无人维护导致技术债务的问题。强调持续维护和更新项目的重要性，而不是不断重新开始新项目，这样可以避免重复劳动和错误。

• **johngossman**：建议工程师需要理解公司的业务和赚钱方式，主动与上层管理人员、销售和支持人员沟通，以更好地理解公司需求并调整自己的工作方向。

• **RainyDayTmrw**：虽然不喜欢“对齐”这个术语，但承认其重要性。认为个体贡献者需要与管理层就工作优先级达成一致，即使这不公平。

• **cljacoby**：对文章中的建议持混合态度，认为部分建议是有益的，但也有可能导致“取悦老板”的消极结果，特别是在管理层没有明确方向或优先级频繁变动的情况下。

• **dogleash**：指出文章建议可能适用于缺乏技术领导的项目，但未能提供足够的管理技能培训。认为新手员工需要更有经验的 seniors 指导，而不是仅仅通过取悦管理层来获得晋升。

• **eXpl0it3r**：质疑只关注让高层满意的做法是否会导致低质量的代码和技术债务，强调投资于高质量的代码和文档的重要性。

• **agentultra**：强调公司如果不重视工程师的工作质量，最终会导致安全漏洞、性能问题和客户不满，建议在这种情况下寻找新的工作机会。

• **unwind**：对“skip-level”这个术语感到困惑，并试图澄清其定义和使用方式。

• **highfrequency**：指出上层管理往往缺乏技术洞察力，导致工程师只做最低限度的工​​作来满足OKR，而忽略了工程质量。建议将技术专家推向高层，以确保高质量的工作。

• **nyanpasu64**：用Google不断推出新聊天应用的例子来讽刺大公司频繁推出新产品而不是专注于完善现有产品的现象。

• **pmarreck**：指出除非是自己销售产品或服务，否则工程师很难完全自主地工作，而这可能意味着没有志同道合的同事。

• **davidmurdoch**：讨论了“开发速度工程师”的角​​色，这些工程师通过优化系统和流程来提高团队效率，但往往在裁员时首先被解雇。尽管如此，认为这类工作对组织的效率至关重要。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于工程师是否应该只专注于技术工作，还是需要更多地参与到业务沟通和管理中。
- 另一个讨论点是管理层对技术工作的理解和评价能力，以及如何在取悦管理层和保持技术质量之间取得平衡。
- 工程师在项目完成后的维护责任和长期贡献也是讨论的重要内容。

43903741.article_content:
What does it mean to get things done? In the abstract, you can complete a mathematical proof or a problem set, but the real world is much fuzzier. Suppose I plant a tree in my backyard. Once the sapling is in the ground, is that done? Not really. There’s always more work to do: clearing the ground around it, watering, keeping pests away, pruning, and so on. Programming large web applications is more like planting a tree than completing a mathematical proof. Once you write a service, you can keep working on it forever if you want to.
In large tech companies, this fact is a trap for competent but unagentic engineers. They see an infinite queue of tasks that they’re capable of doing, and they start delivering a stream of marginal improvements to a particular subsystem
1
. From their perspective, it feels like they’re crushing it. After all, they’re putting out work at their top speed: no downtime, no waiting on other teams. But they’re not doing their actual job, which is to deliver the most value they can to their company. From the perspective of their manager and skip-level, they’re not getting anything done.
What does it mean to get things done in large companies? Most importantly, it means
finishing
things. How can you finish things in a world where you can keep improving systems indefinitely? It means
getting them to a point where the decision-makers at the company are happy
. At that point, you have to declare victory and walk away! Go and do something else! I’ve seen many engineers stick around delivering one more tweak or one more refactor - long past the point where their work stopped being perceived as a successful project and started being perceived as wasted time. Better to deliver two more things in that time.
Second, it means delivering the kind of things that are
legible
to the decision-makers at the company: i.e. visible to your manager, plus 1-3 skip levels, depending on your title. The easiest way to do this is to deliver things that they already know about, such as projects that they’ve asked you to do, or incidents that are serious enough that they’re involved in them. It’s possible to make other work legible to them as well. If your work produces or saves money, that will make it immediately legible, for instance (or you could just be really convincing). By default, work you do isn’t legible: to the decision-makers, it’s generic technical nonsense. They don’t know whether it’s crucial high-impact work or pointless code reshuffling, and will tend to assume the latter.
In short, getting things done means getting them in a state where:
(a) executives at the company understand what’s happened, and
(b) are happy with it
To many, this will be an unsatisfying definition of what it means to get things done. Lots of engineers will want a more solid definition than “it’s a social construct”. However, as someone with a philosophy background, I have a healthy respect for social constructs. The concept “chair” is a social construct, and chairs are plenty real[2]. In some ways, “getting things done” is even more real. It can pay your rent! If you don’t respect it, it can even get you fired.
Summary
Just because you’re doing work doesn’t mean you’re getting things done
Nothing is ever “done” in the non-abstract world. Everything can be worked on indefinitely
If you want to get things done you can’t be a gardener. You have to aim for a bullet-point list of achievements
So what’s “done” mean in that context? It means the company is happy with the state of it
Declare victory and walk away: go and do something else!
In the ideal case, that is. In the non-ideal case, they make a series of changes that suit their personal taste but have no real customer impact.
↩
For much more on this, you can go and (somehow) find my favourite book of underappreciated moral philosophy,
Moral Notions
by Julius Kovesi.
↩

data.title: Design and evaluation of a parrot-to-parrot video-calling system (2023)
data.author: michalpleban
data.article_summary: 研究表明，宠物鹦鹉可以通过视频通话与同类互动，从而获得积极的体验。在美国，约有2000万只宠物鸟可能感到孤独，而这种视频交流为它们提供了社交机会。实验中，15只鹦鹉学会了发起视频通话，并在两个月内进行了147次通话。它们表现出理解对方是真实活鸟，并学到新技能如飞行和发声。鹦鹉们建立了友谊，频繁互call，显示出类似人类社交的互惠关系。虽然视频通话不能完全替代野外社交，但对被圈养的鹦鹉有显著改善作用，尤其是无法进行面对面互动的鸟。不过，研究人员提醒，主人需谨慎监控通话，以防负面反应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宠物鸟类的智能行为以及它们与科技产品的互动

不同观点：
• **bArray** 分享了自己的雄性超级鹦鹉能够滑动YouTube视频，选择播放包含鸟类的视频，并提到该鸟还会乞食和表现出对高蛋白食物的强烈需求，甚至会尝试模仿人类 speech。bArray 还提出希望能让鹦鹉通过技术手段与其他鸟类交流。
  
• **Zobat** 提到有人训练鹦鹉通过声音控制笼子的灯光，结果发现鹦鹉希望比人类设定的时间更早关灯，显示出鹦鹉有自己的作息需求。这表明鹦鹉有能力通过技术手段表达自己的意愿。

• **srean** 强调鹦鹉和鸦科鸟类的智力，并推荐阅读相关书籍（如《Alex & Me》），但并未直接回应具体行为，而是从科学和认知角度讨论这些鸟类的智能。

• **duxup** 引述了一位在鹦鹉救助机构工作的人的经验，指出鹦鹉有时像小孩一样，有破坏性倾向，喜欢拆解物品，这与 bArray 的观察部分呼应，尤其是对鹦鹉行为的描述。

• **teddyh** 以幽默的方式提出可以让鹦鹉接管Twitter，间接回应了 bArray 关于鹦鹉使用技术手段交流的想法，但更多是调侃而非实际建议。

• **rwmj** 认为需要开发一个适合鹦鹉使用的输入设备和自动化系统来帮助它们完成交流，这直接回应了 bArray 关于让鹦鹉与其他鸟类交流的愿望。

• **mncharity** 提供了关于鹦鹉认知的最新研究链接，并通过AI搜索展示了与鹦鹉视觉情感分析相关的发展，提供了科学依据，但没有直接讨论具体行为。

• **imglorp** 提出可以建立一个让鸟类能够随时社交的平台，甚至训练一个“鸟类聊天机器人”来与鸟类互动，这进一步扩展了 bArray 关于鹦鹉技术交流的想法。

• **gadders** 分享了自己狗和同事狗在视频通话中互相吠叫的经历，虽然不确定它们是否在传递信息，但这显示了动物之间可能存在某种形式的互动。

• **deadbabe** 提到自己驯养了一只乌鸦，它会通过AI帮助解决简单的任务，这展示了鸦科鸟类的智能，但与 bArray 的鹦鹉经验不同。

• **thimkerbell** 对视频内容表示怀疑，虽然没有详细说明原因，但这引入了对 bArray 所描述行为的真实性和可信度的争议。

• **CalRobert** 关心视频播放客户端是否为开源软件，显示出对技术实现细节的关注，而并非直接讨论鹦鹉的行为。

• **benob** 提出实验中是否使用了镜子或简单录音作为基线，质疑实验设计的严谨性，间接对 bArray 的观察提出了科学上的质疑。

• **TZubiri** 通过与AI助手的对话，探讨了鸟类视觉颜色的问题，并指出鸟类如鹦鹉的视觉系统类似于人类的RGB系统，而狗只有两种颜色锥体，这为鸟类与技术互动提供了科学背景。

• 争议焦点之一是 bArray 描述的鹦鹉行为的真实性和可信度，尤其是 thimkerbell 的怀疑态度和 benob 对实验设计的质疑。
• 另一个讨论点是科技如何帮助鹦鹉实现更多交流和互动，包括 rwmj 提出的输入设备和 imglorp 的“鸟类聊天机器人”设想。
• 对鸟类智能的科学研究和实际观察结果也是讨论的重要部分，srean 和 mncharity 提供了相关文献和研究链接，以支持对鸟类智能的理解。

43903728.article_content:
Ellie, an 11-year-old Goffin’s cockatoo, video chats with a friend.
Matthew Modoono / Northeastern University
When humans are feeling lonely, we can call or video chat with friends and family who live far away. But, scientists asked, what about pet parrots? New research suggests that these chatty creatures may also benefit from virtually connecting with their peers.
Domesticated
parrots
that learned to initiate video chats with other pet parrots had a variety of positive experiences, such as learning new skills, researchers from Northeastern University, the University of Glasgow and MIT report this month in
Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
.
“She came alive during the calls,” one pet parent said about their bird, according to a Northeastern University
statement
.
The idea for this study was not random:
In the wild
, parrots tend to live in large flocks. But when kept in captivity, such as in people’s homes as pets, these social birds are often on their own. Feeling bored and isolated, they may develop psychological issues and can even resort to self-harming tendencies like plucking out their feathers.
Lonely parrots are unhappy parrots, so researchers set out to find a way for some of the estimated 20 million pet birds living in the United States to connect with each other. They recruited volunteers from Parrot Kindergarten, an online training program for parrot owners and their beloved pets.
Lonely Parrots Flock Together with Video-Calling Technology
Watch on
During the first two weeks of the study, owners taught their birds to ring a bell, then touch an image of another pet parrot on a tablet screen to initiate a video call. In this initial phase, the participating birds made 212 video calls while their owners carefully monitored their behavior. Owners terminated calls as soon as the birds stopped paying attention to the screen and capped their duration at five minutes. Though 18 parrots began the experiment, three dropped out.
Once the birds had learned how to initiate video interactions, the second phase of the experiment could begin. In this “open call” period, the 15 participating birds could make calls freely; they also got to choose which bird to dial up. Over the next two months, pet parrots made 147 deliberate video calls to other birds. Their owners took detailed notes about the calls and recorded more than 1,000 hours of video footage that the researchers analyzed.
For starters, they found that the parrots took advantage of the opportunity to call one another, and they typically stayed on the call for the maximum time allowed during the experiment. They also seemed to understand that another live bird was on the other side of the screen, not a recorded bird, researchers say. Some of the parrots learned new skills from their virtual companions, including flying, foraging and how to make new sounds.
“I was quite surprised at the range of different behaviors,” co-author
Ilyena Hirskyj-Douglas
, an animal-computer interaction researcher at the University of Glasgow, tells the
Guardian
’s Hannah Devlin. “Some would sing, some would play around and go upside down, others would want to show another bird their toys.” Two weak, older macaws, for example, became very close and even called out to one another “Hi! Come here! Hello!” from their respective screens.
The birds forged strong friendships, which researchers measured by how frequently they chose to call the same individual. Parrots who initiated the highest number of video calls also received the most calls, which suggests a “reciprocal dynamic similar to human socialization,” per the statement.
The experiment also brought parrots and humans closer together—on both sides of the screen. Some birds were even reported to have developed attachments to the human caretakers of their virtual friends.
The birds learned some new behaviors while video chatting with their friends.
Matthew Modoono / Northeastern University
Video chatting can’t replace the social interactions that would occur in the wild, but it may be a viable option for improving the lives of parrots that are already in captivity, the researchers note. In addition, it may be beneficial for birds that cannot interact in person. Pet parrots are highly susceptible to a deadly disease called
avian ganglioneuritis
, which can make it dangerous for human owners to plan in-person parrot playdates.
As for other parrot owners, the researchers caution it might not be wise to suddenly begin launching FaceTime or Zoom chats on behalf of their pets. The study involved experienced parrot handlers who had the time and energy to keep tabs on their birds’ behavior—at the first sign of fear, aggression, disinterest or discomfort, they ended the calls. As the study’s authors note in the statement, “unmediated interactions could lead to fear [or] even violence and property damage.”

data.title: OpenAI reaches agreement to buy Windsurf for around $3B
data.author: tasn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI以30亿美元收购Windsurf和Cursor的合理性及未来影响

不同观点：
• Androider认为Windsurf和Cursor只是临时解决方案，Microsoft已经开始通过锁定VSCode上游代码库来限制这些 fork 的发展。他们可能会在一年内复制这些工具的功能，并提供更高的稳定性和完善性。同时，AI助理功能存在许多bug，工具的核心价值在于更智能的队友而非编辑器。
• bko强调Windsurf从创立到被收购的时间线和融资情况，质疑其价值更多来自于模型还是工具。他认为大部分价值来自底层模型，工具部分可以视作VSCode插件。
• crimsonnoodle58批评这一收购，认为Windsurf只是一个IDE的fork，且Microsoft通过使其最佳扩展不兼容fork来削弱其竞争力。
• owendarko指出，未来的IDE不需要为“AI/vibe coding”切换，AI编码代理应作为IDE的一项功能，而非独立的软件。Microsoft已经开始通过Copilot实现这一功能。
• fcanesin提到OpenAI收购Windsurf可能是为了应对Google的Gemini，以防止用户流失。
• ujkhsjkdhf234质疑这一收购是否为资金浪费，认为OpenAI应有能力以更低成本构建类似工具。
• bix6通过财务数据对比，认为这一收购的市盈率较高。
• ashvardanian认为此次收购更多是为了获取大规模训练数据，而非简单的产品整合，可能对Windsurf的付费客户不利。
• lolinder建议Cursor和Windsurf合作应对Microsoft的威胁，通过与VSCodium和Open VSX市场合作，构建更强大的生态系统。
• bradley13批评并购活动需要更严格监管，以防止垄断。
• resters认为此次收购表明OpenAI在产品开发上的不足，并相信高效的编码助理LLM将成为 commodity，UI/工具锁定是好的投资。
• incorrecthorse同样认为OpenAI可以以更低成本构建类似工具。
• remoroid对Windsurf的使用体验不佳，指出其AI助理功能存在问题。

补充讨论：
• 收购的合理性和工具的实际价值是讨论的焦点，部分评论者质疑收购价格过高，部分则关注工具的功能和底层模型价值。
• Microsoft的竞争策略和其对VSCode生态的影响是另一个重要议题，部分评论者担心Microsoft通过限制扩展来削弱fork的竞争力。
• 合作与生态系统建设被认为是应对Microsoft竞争的潜在策略。

data.title: Sea snail teeth top Kevlar, titanium as strongest material (2015)
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 英国研究人员发现，帽贝（一种海洋蜗牛）的牙齿拥有世界上最强的生物材料，其强度甚至超过凯夫拉纤维和钛。这些牙齿长约一毫米，包含一种称为针铁矿的矿物纤维，使牙齿异常坚固。帽贝利用这些牙齿刮取岩石表面的藻类为食。此前，蜘蛛丝被认为是最强生物材料，但帽贝牙齿的强度是蜘蛛丝的10倍。研究人员认为，这种天然材料的结构可能启发未来在航空、赛车和电子产品中的应用。研究结果发表于《Journal of the Royal Society Interface》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同材料的强度特性及其在实际应用中的挑战

不同观点：
• [gweinberg] 认为材料在压缩和拉伸下的强度并不一定相同。例如，牙齿主要需要在压缩下表现出色，而蜘蛛丝则需要在拉伸下很强。该评论强调了材料在不同应力条件下的性能差异。

• [CGMthrowaway] 指出，goethite矿物纤维的强度只有在纳米级别（400-800纳米）时才表现优异，如果纤维变大，其强度会下降。这提出了在人类应用中复制这种材料的一个挑战，即尺度问题。

• [CRANQonX] 通过个人经验（尝试从岩石上移除这些东西）来支持材料强度的观点，暗示实际生活中的观察支持这种材料的强度特性。

• [andrewinardeer] 关心的是该领域的研究进展，特别是过去十年是否有任何突破，暗示对实际应用进展的关注。

• [coolThingsFirst] 以幽默的方式（牙医发现五个蛀牙）回应，暗示对牙齿强度和材料应用的讨论不以为然，可能认为该话题与实际生活问题关联不大。

• [AdrianB1] 批评将goethite与kevlar和钛进行比较的合理性，认为kevlar和钛并不是在其各自类别中最强的材料，因此这样的比较不科学。这表明了对材料比较方法的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 材料在不同应力条件下的表现差异是讨论的一个重点（[gweinberg]）。
• 纳米尺度下的材料性能问题被提出，作为实际应用中的一个技术难题（[CGMthrowaway]）。
• 有人对该领域的研究进展表示关注，特别是实际应用的可行性（[andrewinardeer]）。
• 对材料比较的科学性和合理性存在争议，特别是与kevlar和钛的比较（[AdrianB1]）。

As It Happens
Sea snail teeth top Kevlar, titanium as world’s strongest material
When you think of a sea snail, you might think slow, but do you think strong? It turns out sea snails contain the strongest material in the world -- in their teeth.
CBC Radio
·
Posted: Feb 19, 2015 3:09 PM EST | Last Updated: February 23, 2015
An image of limpet teeth captured using a scanning electron microscope.
(Photo courtesy of University of Portsmouth)
Social Sharing
British researchers have discovered the world’s strongest biological material ever tested: sea snail teeth.
Yep, you read that right. The super-strong structure of limpet teeth -- a shelled sea mollusc about 5 cm in length -- is so formidable that it could one day be mimicked and used in next-generation airplanes, racing cars and electronics.
“They’re stronger than any man-made material, such as
Kevlar
fibres that are used in bullet-proof vests,”
Asa
Barber, the study’s lead author, tells
As It Happens
host Carol Off.
A close-up of a limpet snail.
(Photo courtesy of the University of Portsmouth)
​
Barber says the teeth, which are about a
millimetre
in length, contain thin fibres of a mineral known as
goethite
.
The limpet requires these strong teeth to feed, as they rasp over rock surfaces to scrape algae off the surface and into their mouths.
Scanning electron micrograph of a limpet tooth.
(Photo courtesy of University of Portsmouth)
Spider silk was previously considered to be the world’s strongest biological material -- limpet teeth are about 10 times as strong.
The full study was recently published in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface
.

AnuDB
AnuDB is a lightweight, serverless document database designed for C++ applications, offering efficient storage of JSON documents through MessagePack serialization. It provides a serverless, schema-less solution for applications requiring flexible data management with robust query capabilities.
Since AnuDB written on top of RocksDB, it ensures atomicity, durability and consistency of your documents. You can adjust memory/CPU usage of AnuDB based on RocksDB options mentioned in
StorageEngine.cpp
and
StorageEngine.h
.Based on these configurations, you can get your desired performance results tailored to your specific platform requirements.
Get Started with AnuDB!
Ready to try AnuDB for your project? Follow these simple steps to get started quickly:
Install AnuDB
See the
installation guide
to set up AnuDB on your machine.
Explore Example Code
Check out our
usage examples
to understand how to interact with AnuDB.
Start Building!
Dive right in by using AnuDB in your application and start storing your data with lightning-fast speed.
Docker Support
AnuDB supports Docker! Run AnuDB in a containerized environment with ease. See our
Docker setup guide
to get started.
MQTT Support
AnuDB integrates seamlessly with MQTT, enabling real-time data communication between devices and servers. If you're working on IoT or real-time messaging systems, AnuDB's MQTT support will make your job easier. Check out our
MQTT integration guide
to get started with MQTT and AnuDB.
Benchmark
Features
Embedded & Serverless
: Run directly within your application with no separate server process required
Embedded Platform Support
: Specifically designed for both standard Linux/Windows systems and embedded platforms
Faster Writes
– RocksDB (LSM-tree) backend is optimized for high-speed inserts/updates.
JSON Document Storage
: Store and query complex JSON documents
RocksDB Backend
: Built on RocksDB for high performance and durability
Transactional Properties
: Inherits atomic operations and configurable durability from RocksDB
Compression Options
: Support for ZSTD compression to reduce storage footprint
Flexible Querying
: Support for equality, comparison, logical operators and sorting
Indexing
: Create indexes to speed up queries on frequently accessed fields
Update Operations
: Rich set of document modification operations
Import/Export
: Easy JSON import and export for data migration. Exported JSON file can be also used to migrate data to Postgresql/SQL sever/MySQL/Oracle DB
C++11 Compatible
: Designed to support a wide range of embedded devices efficiently
Windows/Linux Support
: Designed for Windows/Linux environments and embedded Linux platforms
MQTT Interface
: Connect and operate via MQTT protocol from various platforms
High Concurrency
: Supports 32 concurrent nng worker threads(configurable using
CONCURRENT_THREADS
) for handling MQTT requests
TLS Security
: Secure communications using mbedTLS for encrypted MQTT connections
Cloud MQTT Support
: Compatible with major cloud MQTT brokers
ACID Compliance
: AnuDB inherits atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability from RocksDB

AnuDB now supports interaction via MQTT protocol, allowing you to connect and operate the database from various platforms without direct C++ integration. The implementation uses nlohmann::json for JSON handling.

data.title: RK3588 – Implementing a Vectorscope for processing video in real time
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了在RK3588平台上实现实时矢量示波器以可视化HDMI输入视频流的色度信息的过程。主要挑战包括从视频帧中高效提取UV（色度）数据并避免影响视频播放性能。通过使用RGA3硬件加速器将RGB帧转换为NV12/NV16格式，减少了色彩空间转换的开销。随后，UV数据被导入OpenGL ES纹理用于进一步处理。为了实时计算UV直方图，作者采用了计算着色器（compute shaders），尽管相关文档稀缺，最终成功实现三段式计算管道。最后，通过借鉴OBS插件的渲染方法，实现了不干扰视频播放的矢量示波器可视化，并成功处理1080p@60视频流。该工作在ROCK 5B开发板上完成，运行定制的Ubuntu系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用RK3588或Orange Pi 5 Plus作为HDMI分析器或音频提取器的可行性及其实际应用

不同观点：
• 3abiton认为Orange Pi 5 Plus可以通过其两个HDMI输出端口分别输出视频和音频流，并希望将其用作游戏机的"音频提取器"，将输入的HDMI信号分离成视频和音频两部分。他认为利用HDMI输入功能可以实现这一目的，并对该想法表示兴趣。

• kamma4434则关注实时显示矢量示波器（vectorscope）的必要性，质疑是否有必要在每一帧都进行计算和显示。他提出，由于图像帧与帧之间的变化不大，可以每隔几帧计算和显示一次，以减少计算压力，并且认为观众不会注意到这种变化。

补充讨论：
• 3abiton的评论中提到了实际硬件的使用场景（Orange Pi 5 Plus）及其潜在功能（HDMI输入和输出），并具体描述了将其用作音频提取器的设想。

• kamma4434的评论则集中在对实时显示技术需求的探讨，特别是对矢量示波器在实际应用中计算频率的质疑，提出了通过降低计算频率来优化性能的建议。

争议焦点：
• 3abiton对Orange Pi 5 Plus用作音频提取器的可行性持乐观态度，而kamma4434则对实时显示技术（如矢量示波器）的必要性提出质疑，关注计算资源的合理利用。两者的讨论反映了在硬件多功能应用和实时计算需求上的不同关注点。

43871601.article_content:
Following on from my previous
post
covering decoding and rendering HDMI input on the RK3588, I encountered a new requirement: implementing a real-time vectorscope to visualize chrominance information from the video stream. This proved to be a challenging task due to the need for efficient frame processing and rendering without impacting video playback performance.
Extracting UV Data from Video Frames
The challenges to overcome were:
Accessing U and V (chrominance) values for every pixel in the video stream.
For RGB-formatted frames, a costly color space conversion (RGB to YUV) is required.
The processing overhead increases significantly with higher-resolution frames.
To minimize CPU overhead and offload the color space conversion, I utilized
RGA3
, which efficiently converts each RGB frame into NV12 or NV16 format. This step significantly reduces the processing time needed to access UV data.
Once converted, the UV plane needed to be imported into an
OpenGL ES texture
for further processing and visualization. To preserve performance and avoid unnecessary memory copies, the goal was to directly bind the UV data as a texture.
Computing the UV Histogram
The primary processing here
Computing a UV histogram in real time based on pixel data from the video frame.
Normalizing the histogram values so it scales properly regardless of resolution or luminance.
Building a real-time UV histogram from each frame requires scanning and processing a large volume of pixel data efficiently. Traditional OpenGL fragment shaders are not well-suited for this type of arbitrary data accumulation, especially when dealing with high-resolution video.
Given that the
Mali G-610 GPU
is compliant with
OpenGL ES 3.1
, I explored the use of
compute shaders
, a more flexible approach for performing general-purpose GPU (GPGPU) operations like histogram generation.
Compute shaders for OpenGL ES is sparsely documented, and practical usage examples, especially for embedded platforms are limited. As a result, much of the development involved experimentation and iterative debugging, making it feel like a bit of a black art. Finally I managed to chain to together 3 compute shaders each perform one step in the pipeline.
Rendering the Vectorscope Output
The final step involved visualizing the processed chroma data in a way that mirrors a traditional vectorscope. This required overlaying the normalized UV histogram along with reference markers without disrupting video playback.
I drew inspiration from the
OBS monitor plugin
, which includes a vectorscope feature. Its rendering approach informed how I structured the visualization pipeline, particularly around how histogram data is mapped to screen coordinates.
The demo video shows the Vectorscope is capable of processing a 1080p@60 video stream.
Work was carried out on a ROCK 5B board running a tailored Ubuntu image maintained by
Joshua Riek
.

data.title: FUTO
data.author: ahaferburg
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一家致力于开发和资助以用户隐私和控制为核心的技术和软件的组织——FUTO，及其相关项目。这些项目包括FUTO键盘（保护隐私的安卓键盘）、GrayJay（关注创作者的视频应用）、immich（高性能自托管的照片和视频管理工具）、FUTO Voice（保护隐私的语音输入应用）、Polycentric（分布式社交网络）、Harbor（保护网络身份的应用）等。此外，FUTO还支持多个开源项目和资助计划，旨在让技术回归用户掌控，包括与Signal、Tor Project等组织的合作。

data.title: Show HN: ProcASM – A general purpose, visual programming lanugage
data.author: Temdog007
data.article_summary:
ProcASM是一种通用的可视化编程语言，主要概念是过程（Procedures），由一系列通过信号连接的子过程（Sub-Procedures）组成。子过程执行创建、修改或删除数据的任务。状态机是过程的实例，执行到让位任务时暂停，保存变量并在暂停处恢复执行。开发者使用预定义任务实现算法，无需编写代码。

主要功能包括：
- 集成开发环境（IDE），用于创建过程和子过程，检测错误。
- 无需编译的解释器，支持暂停/恢复、查看状态机及其值、设置断点和监视变量。
- 可导出过程的视觉显示（SVG、DOT格式），并转译为C/C++代码。
- 无垃圾收集或引用计数，使用工作队列处理并发状态机执行。
- 项目比较器生成HTML文件，描述两个项目之间的差异。

提供在线试用和文档，帮助开发者入门和了解更多信息。

不同观点：

• nizarmah 则关注用户体验，尤其是与MIT的Scratch相比，认为该编程工具的用户界面过于复杂，不够直观。他建议引入类似Scratch的模块化设计，通过可视化块状结构让用户更容易上手，并提出可以通过映射输入/输出流来连接不同的模块。他还提到希望该工具能够像玩具一样简单易用，并具有可重用的模块库，以便用户可以快速原型化项目。

补充讨论：
• mdaniel的观点聚焦于订阅模式的经济性和公平性，认为编程语言工具的订阅费用如果不提供持续价值（如更新），则不应强制收费。

• nizarmah的观点则强调用户体验和易用性，建议通过模块化和可视化设计降低使用门槛，使工具更具吸引力和易于上手。他提出了具体的设计建议，如块状结构和模块库的实现方式。

• 争议的焦点在于如何在商业模式和用户体验之间找到平衡。mdaniel认为当前的订阅模式不合理，而nizarmah则关注如何通过设计改进提升用户体验。两者都反映了用户对编程工具在使用便捷性和经济性上的高要求。

Procedures as State Machines (ProcASM)
A general purpose, visual programming language designed for desktop computers.
The only major concept in this language are Procedures (no Data Structures, Enumerations, Functions, etc). Procedures are a series of Sub-Procedures connected through Signals. Sub-Procedures are a series of tasks that create, modify, or delete data. State Machines are instances of Procedures. State Machines execute until they reach a yield task. Then, they store the requested variables and will resume at the point it previously stopped.
Instead of writing code, developers use a set of pre-defined tasks to implement algorithms. See
documentation
for more details.

data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 《Modern LaTeX》是一份简明的LaTeX指南，旨在避免过时的内容，帮助用户快速上手这一排版工具。指南提供了LaTeX的安装和使用方法，推荐使用LuaLaTeX进行编译，并介绍了如何调整字体和解决交叉引用问题。用户可以通过提供的源码构建文档，并根据需要自定义字体设置。指南的正式版本使用多种字体类型，用户可根据实际情况修改。反馈和贡献可通过GitHub页面提交。最新版本可在链接下载：https://assets.bitbashing.io/modern-latex.pdf。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LaTeX及其现代替代品的比较与选择

不同观点：
• BlackFly认为LaTeX应与HTML+CSS+JavaScript等网页技术比较，而非Word。他质疑LaTeX的现代化程度，并建议增加响应式设计以适应在线阅读需求。
• dev_l1x_be和多位其他用户（如iNic、__mharrison__）推荐Typst作为LaTeX的现代替代品，强调其编译速度快、语法简洁、工具支持好等优点，但也提到用户群体相对较少。
• dochtman简单表示Typst是现代的LaTeX，附上链接支持其观点。
• herewulf计划从Org mode转到LaTeX来制作多语言CV，寻求模板建议，并分享了一个正在实验的项目链接。
• qiu3344认为LaTeX尽管有缺点，但仍然非常方便和强大，并提到pandoc的Markdown作为另一种选择。
• agubelu对LaTeX有复杂的情感，既感激学过它，但又庆幸可以不再使用它。
• watusername推荐Tectonic作为一体化的LaTeX工具链，提到其单执行文件和懒加载TeX Live的优点，但对其选择XeTeX而非LuaTeX表示遗憾。
• aquafox基于自身PhD写作经验，认为Quarto是更易用的选择，尤其适合技术协作较少的场景。
• arthur-st分享了LaTeX工具链的未来趋势，建议使用VSCode及其扩展、TeX Live和LuaTeX。
• agoose77推广MyST Engine，强调其通过Markdown处理结构化数据的能力。
• cess11推荐LyX作为图形化编辑器，认为其适合新手，且在需要时仍可下潜到LaTeX进行高级定制。
• rochak分享了学习LaTeX的痛苦经历，甚至因此放弃了研究工作。

补充讨论：
• LaTeX的现代化问题和响应式设计需求是讨论的一个焦点。BlackFly和部分其他用户对LaTeX的现代化程度提出质疑，认为应增加对在线阅读和响应式设计的支持。
• 多种LaTeX替代品被提及，尤其是Typst和Quarto，用户对其优点和缺点进行了详细比较。
• 工具链和编译速度是另一个讨论重点，Tectonic和LyX被作为更易用的选择推荐。
• 个人使用经验和情感因素在讨论中也起到重要作用，部分用户对LaTeX有复杂的情感，既感激其功能又对其使用难度感到困扰。

Modern LaTeX
LaTeX is a tool for creating beautiful writing, or a torture device that drives
users to the brink of madness every time they see bad spacing for the rest
of their lives. One of the two. Despite origins that can be traced back four
decades, it remains one of the best typesetting programs around. Many of its
guides, however, haven't aged as well. This short book will get you started with
LaTeX without bogging you down in arcana that lost its relevance back in the 90s.
Where do I get it?
An up-to-date version should be available at
https://assets.bitbashing.io/modern-latex.pdf
How do I build it?
Install LuaLaTeX, a modern, Unicode-aware version of LaTeX.
On Linux, this is usually as simple as installing your distro's TeX Live
package, e.g.,
texlive-base
or
texlive-core
.
The same package should also provide the
latexmk
script.
(See below)
Check out the
online
branch of the source repository,
which is optimized for digital display instead of a printed book.
Changes include even margins, centered page numbers, a lack of blank pages
between chapters, and so on.
Change the fonts as-needed.
The official version of this book is typeset with Garamond Premier,
Neue Haas Grotesk, URW Futura, Drive Mono, Noto, and (of course) Latin Modern.
In the likely case that you don't have all of these typefaces,
change the
fontspec
commands (e.g.,
setmainfont
, etc.) appropriately,
then modify or remove the colophon at the back of the book.
Build the book using
latexmk -lualatex -latexoption=-halt-on-error modern-latex.tex
Note that
latexmk
will run LuaLaTeX multiple times, since
TeX generates cross references in one pass, then links them in a second.
If you can't use
latexmk
for some reason, you can manually invoke
lualatex -halt-on-error -shell-escape modern-latex.tex
until it no longer warns,
"Label(s) may have changed. Rerun to get cross-references right."
Feedback
...is welcome!
Please issue pull requests on this book's Github page,
or contact the author via matt <at> bitbashing.io
Enjoy!

• BlackFly认为LaTeX应与HTML+CSS+JavaScript等网页技术比较，而非Word。他质疑LaTeX的现代化程度，并建议增加响应式设计以适应在线阅读需求。
• dev_l1x_be和多位其他用户（如iNic、__mharrison__）推荐Typst作为LaTeX的现代替代品，强调其编译速度快、语法简洁、工具支持好等优点，但也提到用户群体相对较少。
• dochtman简单表示Typst是现代的LaTeX，附上链接支持其观点。
• herewulf计划从Org mode转到LaTeX来制作多语言CV，寻求模板建议，并分享了一个正在实验的项目链接。
• qiu3344认为LaTeX尽管有缺点，但仍然非常方便和强大，并提到pandoc的Markdown作为另一种选择。
• agubelu对LaTeX有复杂的情感，既感激学过它，但又庆幸可以不再使用它。
• watusername推荐Tectonic作为一体化的LaTeX工具链，提到其单执行文件和懒加载TeX Live的优点，但对其选择XeTeX而非LuaTeX表示遗憾。
• aquafox基于自身PhD写作经验，认为Quarto是更易用的选择，尤其适合技术协作较少的场景。
• arthur-st分享了LaTeX工具链的未来趋势，建议使用VSCode及其扩展、TeX Live和LuaTeX。
• agoose77推广MyST Engine，强调其通过Markdown处理结构化数据的能力。
• cess11推荐LyX作为图形化编辑器，认为其适合新手，且在需要时仍可下潜到LaTeX进行高级定制。
• rochak分享了学习LaTeX的痛苦经历，甚至因此放弃了研究工作。

data.author: elpocko
data.article_summary: 文章报道了一起针对Linux服务器和开发环境的供应链攻击，攻击者将磁盘擦除恶意软件隐藏在GitHub上的Golang模块中。这三个恶意模块使用高度混淆的代码下载并执行一个名为"done.sh"的Bash脚本，该脚本利用"dd"命令对主存储卷（/dev/sda）进行数据覆盖，导致不可逆的数据丢失和系统崩溃。攻击专门针对Linux环境，确认运行环境为Linux后执行擦除操作。这三个模块已被GitHub下架，但研究人员警告，Go生态系统的去中心化特性使得类似攻击仍有可能发生，开发者需保持警惕。

43903099.article_content:
Linux wiper malware hidden in malicious Go modules on GitHub
By
Ionut Ilascu
May 6, 2025
05:13 AM
0
A supply-chain attack targets Linux servers with disk-wiping malware hidden in Golang modules published on GitHub.
The campaign was detected last month and relied on three malicious Go modules that included “highly obfuscated code” for retrieving remote payloads and executing them.
Complete disk destruction
The attack appears designed specifically for Linux-based servers and developer environments, as the destructive payload - a Bash script named
done.sh
, runs a ‘dd’ command for the file-wiping activity.
Furthermore, the payload verifies that it runs in a Linux environment (
runtime.GOOS == "linux"
) before trying to execute.
An analysis from supply-chain security company Socket shows that the command overwrites with zeroes every byte of data, leading to irreversible data loss and system failure.
The target is the primary storage volume,
/dev/sda
, that holds critical system data, user files, databases, and configurations.
“By populating the entire disk with zeros, the script completely destroys the file system structure, operating system, and all user data, rendering the system unbootable and unrecoverable” -
Socket
The researchers discovered the attack in April and identified three Go modules on GitHub, that have since been removed from the platform:
github[.]com/truthfulpharm/prototransform
github[.]com/blankloggia/go-mcp
github[.]com/steelpoor/tlsproxy
All three modules contained obfuscated code that decodes into commands that use ‘wget’ to download the malicious data-wiping script (/bin/bash or /bin/sh).
According to Socket researchers, the payloads are executed immediately after download, “leaving virtually no time for response or recovery.”
The malicious Go modules appear to have impersonated legitimate projects for converting message data to various formats (Prototransform), a Go implementation of the Model Context Protocol (go-mcp), and a TLS proxy tool that provides encryption for TCP and HTTP servers (tlsproxy).
Socket researchers warn that even minimal exposure to the analyzed destructive modules can significantly impact such as complete data loss.
Because of the decentralized nature of the Go ecosystem that lacks proper checks, packages from different developers can have the same or similar names.
Attackers can leverage this to create module namespaces that appear legitimate and wait for developers to integrate the malicious code into their projects.

data.title: Hugo Administrators Resign in Wake of ChatGPT Controversy
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 2025年西雅图Worldcon年会前，三名组委会领导因使用生成式AI（LLM）审核大会嘉宾的争议而辞职。尽管雨果奖本身未受影响，但使用ChatGPT引发社区强烈反应，甚至导致入围作者Yoon Ha Lee撤回其作品《Moonstorm》。组委会主席Kathy Bond为此道歉，但事件已在社交媒体上引起轩然大波。年会将于8月举行，雨果奖将在8月16日颁发。

Another year
,
yet
another
Hugo Awards-adjacent controversy
? That might be what fans of sci-fi lit and related media are thinking, with news today that a trio of leaders from the Seattle 2025 Worldcon, the upcoming iteration of the convention where the Hugos are annually presented, have resigned. This year, at least, the awards themselvesâvoted on by members of the World Science Fiction Society (WSFS)âseemingly aren’t directly involved in the dust-up.
In a
post on Bluesky
co-signed by Hugo administrator Nicholas Whyte, deputy Hugo administrator Esther MacCallum-Stewart, and World Science Fiction Society division head Cassidy, the trio announced they were resigning from their roles ahead of the Seattle event, which takes place in August. “We want to reaffirm that no LLMs or generative AI have been used in the Hugo Awards process at any stage,” the statement read in part, which might turn the heads of anyone who is a) interested in the Hugos, but b) not up on the latest controversy.
However, plenty of people in the community are well aware of what’s been going on. A quick journey to
the blog File 770
will bring you up to speed, as will a visit to Seattle Worldcon 2025’s own site, which
on April 30
shared a post clarifying exactly what role AI played in the upcoming event.
“We have received questions regarding Seattleâs use of AI tools in our vetting process for program participants,” Seattle Worldcon 2025 chair Kathy Bond wrote. “In the interest of transparency, we will explain the process of how we are using a Large Language Model (LLM). We understand that members of our community have very reasonable concerns and strong opinions about using LLMs. Please be assured that no data other than a proposed panelistâs name has been put into the LLM script that was used. Letâs repeat that point: no data other than a proposed panelistâs name has been put into the LLM script. The sole purpose of using the LLM was to streamline the online search process used for program participant vetting, and rather than being accepted uncritically, the outputs were carefully analyzed by multiple members of our team for accuracy.”
Bond’s post goes on to explain that “using this process saved literally hundreds of hours of volunteer staff time, and we believe it resulted in more accurate vetting after the step of checking any purported negative results. We have also not utilized an LLM in any other aspect of our program or convention.”
That last line is what today’s resignation post from Whyte, MacCallum-Stewart, and Cassidy also emphasized: that the Hugos themselves were not pulled into this process, which was meant to help Seattle Worldcon 2025 more efficiently compile the panels it offers to convention attendees.
Bond later posted
an additional message
on May 2, re-iterating her apology about using ChatGPT as part of the convention’s program vetting. “Additionally, I regret releasing a statement that did not address the concerns of our community,” she shared. “My initial statement on the use of AI tools in program vetting was incomplete, flawed, and missed the most crucial points. I acknowledge my mistake and am truly sorry for the harm it caused.”
However, as
File 770 pointed out
, the damage has apparently already been done: the use of ChatGPT in any capacity in connection to Worldcon created a furor on social media. It also inspired at least one Hugo nominee to remove their book from contention: Yoon Ha Lee, whose
Moonstorm
was named a Lodestar Award finalist, which honors YA releases. In a May 1 post on
Bluesky
, the author linked to the April 30 Worldcon blog post noted above, and noted he was withdrawing the title from consideration.
Then, in
a post shared today
responding to
File 770’s latest post
announcing the resignations, the author wrote “All respect and I’m grateful to them for their work, sorry [things] came to this pass.”
Seattle Worldcon 2025 takes place August 13-17; the Hugo Awards will be handed out August 16.

data.title: 'Streaming as surveillance': How Spotify is poisoning music in the digital age
data.author: internet_points
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了Spotify的崛起及其对音乐产业的影响，聚焦于技术资本主义对音乐创作、消费和文化的负面效应。作者Liz Pelly通过大量采访揭示，Spotify及其类似平台将音乐变成广告工具，剥削艺术家，降低音乐的文化价值。文章批评Spotify的版税制度不公，大艺术家获利远超独立音乐人。同时，Spotify鼓励用户被动消费音乐，削弱了主动聆听和音乐的情感连接。文章警示，音乐产业正被科技巨头操控，艺术家和消费者成为牺牲品，音乐创作逐渐失去灵魂，变得商品化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：付费墙（paywall）机制的使用和影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：对付费墙的支持  
  ∟ 论据：内容创作需要资金支持，付费墙是合理的内容变现方式，能够确保高质量内容的持续生产。例如，像《纽约时报》等新闻机构依赖付费墙来维持运营。
  
• 观点二：对付费墙的反对  
  ∟ 论据：付费墙限制了信息的自由获取，尤其对于学生和低收入人群不公平。部分读者认为，广告收入或其他商业模式应该被更多考虑，以保证信息的可获取性。

• 观点三：对付费墙的折中态度  
  ∟ 论据：部分支持者认为可以采用“软付费墙”模式，例如限制每月免费文章数量，这样既能促进内容变现，也能保证一定程度的开放性。读者可以根据需求选择是否订阅。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：付费墙是否损害了公众的知情权，特别是在新闻和学术领域。支持者强调内容创作的价值，反对者则关注信息平等获取的权利。
• 其他模式：讨论了替代付费墙的其他盈利模式，如捐赠模式（例如维基百科）、会员制和众筹等，这些模式能够在一定程度上缓解付费墙带来的问题。
• 对付费墙效果的质疑：一些评论者提到，付费墙可能导致用户流失，因为许多用户不愿意为在线内容付费，进而转向免费替代平台。这可能影响媒体的用户基础和广告收入。

总结：围绕付费墙的讨论主要集中在内容变现与信息自由获取的平衡问题上，不同观点涉及对付费墙的合理性、公平性及其对媒体行业的长远影响。

Mood Machine: The Rise of Spotify and the Cost of the Perfect Playlist
Liz Pelly
Hachette, $32.99
So Spotify knows
Amused to Death
is my favourite Roger Waters album and
Perfect Sense
is my favourite track. I bet it hasn’t worked out which line of the song is stuck on high rotation in my head. Yet.
Perfect Sense
is a tragicomic saga of human folly in which a curious monkey decides to leave the jungle for a more comfortable life. “Mama, mama,” he wails as he realises too late the cost of his evolution, “why do I have to keep reading these technical manuals?”
That’s the line stuck in my head because that’s me, every day of this century. It’s me again, wading through this important, mind-numbingly complicated book about how Spotify is poisoning how we choose, find, make, sell, hear, buy and generally think (or not) about music in the digital age.
Like any monkey, I just want to be amused with a minimum of inconvenience. Hence, Spotify. The fact that its billionaire CEO Daniel Ek is selling my data for shares in war technology while systematically strangling and debasing music as we know it and enslaving the people who make it? Mama, mama, talk about inconvenient.
American music journalist Liz Pelly’s story of the conquest of streaming — it now accounts for 84 per cent of recorded music income; Spotify’s share is 30 per cent— is a horrendous tale of techno-capitalism stamping on the face of humanity. It’s business as usual in a world where our attention is the new gold, just especially galling given the old currencies of heart and soul that traditionally bond musicians and listeners.
Music journalist Liz Pelly.
The very notion of “listening” is ripe for extermination under a system where users are encouraged to “lean back” and let playlist editors or algorithms choose sounds to massage your mood without you worrying your pretty little head which intelligence – artistic, commercial, human, artificial, indentured – is filling the silence.
“Often,” Pelly writes, “conversations about the streaming era centre [on] the way music has been financially devalued. But there is also a broader, harder-to-pin-down cultural devaluation … the relegation of music to something passable, just filling the air to drown out the office workers’ inner thoughts.”
Advertisement
Our passivity is key. Drawn from scores of interviews with former Spotify employees and other biz “insiders”, Pelly’s portrait of an industry gamed by tech bros to turn music into “a traffic source for advertising product” is a classic corporate greed conspiracy with clueless musicians and consumers as patsies. Again.
This heist began with the file-sharing crisis of the early 2000s, when wholesale music piracy (Napster, LimeWire, Pirate Bay et al) spooked major record labels into buying into a gaggle of cowboy streaming services, throwing their artists under the bus in a gallant rush to save “the industry” (i.e., their jobs).
When Spotify emerged as the horse to back, Sony, for instance, received $US25 million plus a slice of the company and millions in advertising to hand over its music for two years, “with no clarification of whether this had to be shared with artists”. Wonder which way that windfall blew?
“The new boss partnered pretty well with the old boss,” as one independent musician/activist says in the book. Spotify’s Byzantine royalties system was soon revealed to be paying indies about one-sixth of the pennies doled out to the majors – though they could buy prestige “playlist” treatment by cutting their share further.
Mama, mama. Good luck keeping up with the Filtr and the Digster, the Tunigo, Songza, Snowfish, Echo Nest and S4A and other systems bloating the new economy of curated playlists, taste profiles, user-consumption data-crunching and “creator tools”. Suffice it to say that with great power comes great responsibility – to ramp up your stock price before the stock float.
Musicians? Spotify discovered these were ideally replaced by “ghost artists” paid off to make muzak for users conditioned to “lean back” and daydream. If a chapter titled “The Conquest of Chill” doesn’t make you shudder in horror, it can only be because you literally can’t tell music from “mood vibes”.
Loading
The news for music lovers is worse. The dominance of Spotify means artists aspiring to a piece of the only pie in town have to play by its rules: making music for inoffensive, made-up genres (love that “aesthetic rap”) and wasting creative time on “content” for whatever new gimmick the boss reckons will boost his traffic.

总结：围绕付费墙的讨论主要集中在内容变现与信息自由获取的平衡问题上，不同观点涉及对付费墙的合理性、公平性及其对媒体行业的长远影响。

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了英特尔的Arrow Lake架构芯片的细节，特别是其小芯片（chiplet）设计。Andreas Schiling分享了Arrow Lake的芯片布局图片，展示了计算模块、IO模块、SoC模块和GPU模块的位置。计算模块采用台积电的N3B工艺，面积为117.241 mm²，而IO和SoC模块使用台积电的较旧N6工艺。所有模块都位于英特尔22nm FinFET工艺的基础模块上。Arrow Lake的一个显著特点是将E核夹在P核之间，以减少热热点。每个P核有3MB的L3缓存，每个E核集群有3MB的L2缓存。尽管这是英特尔首个桌面芯片设计，但由于互联延迟问题，市场反应不佳。英特尔正通过固件更新解决此问题，未来芯片设计将更高效、优化。

43903420.article_content:
(Image credit: Intel)
Die shots of Intel’s Arrow Lake architecture have been published, revealing Intel’s chiplet (tile) infused design in all of its glory.
Andreas Schiling on X
shared several images of Arrow Lake up close, revealing the layout of Arrow Lake’s individual tiles and the layout of the cores inside the compute tile.
The first photo exposes the full die of Intel’s desktop
Core Ultra 200S
series CPUs, with the compute tile on the upper left, the IO tile on the bottom, and the SoC tile and GPU tile on the right. To the bottom left and top right are two filler dies designed to provide structural rigidity.
A few highlights from the deep analysis of #ArrowLake by @highyieldYT pic.twitter.com/WFUG0xVaFE
May 5, 2025
The compute die is fabbed on TSMC’s bleeding-edge
N3B
node, with a total area of 117.241 mm². The IO tile and SoC tile are fabbed on TSMC’s older N6 node, with the IO tile measuring 24.475mm squared and the SoC tile 86.648mm squared. All of the tiles rest on an underlying base tile fabbed on Intel’s 22nm FinFET node. Arrow Lake is the first Intel architecture that is fabricated entirely using nodes from a competitor, except for the base tile.
The next image shows all of the sub-components for the secondary tiles in Arrow Lake. The I/O die houses the
Thunderbolt 4
controller/display PHY, PCIe Express buffers/PHYs, and TBT4 PHYs. The SoC tile houses the display engines, media engine, more PCIe PHYs, buffers, and the DDR5 memory controllers. The GPU tile houses four Xe GPU cores and an Xe LPG (
Arc Alchemist
) render slice.
The final image shows off Intel’s latest core configuration for Arrow Lake, which differs from previous hybrid Intel architectures. For Arrow Lake, Intel opted to sandwich the E-cores between the P-cores rather than putting them all in their own cluster, allegedly to reduce thermal hotspots. Four of the eight P-cores reside on the borders of the die with the other four residing in the middle of the die. The four E-core clusters (which house four cores each) are sandwiched between the outer and inner P-cores.
Schilling’s die shot also exposes the cache layout for Arrow Lake, comprised of 3MB of L3 cache per P-core (36MB in total) and 3MB of L2 cache per E-core cluster, with 1.5MB shared between two cores directly. An interconnect bridges the two L2 cache clusters (and their associated cores) together, which is also responsible for connecting each core cluster to the ring agent. One major upgrade Intel made with Arrow Lake is connecting the E-core clusters to L3 cache shared by the P-cores, effectively giving the E-cores an L3 cache.
Arrow Lake
is one of Intel’s most complex architectures to date and the first from the company to bring a chiplet-style design to the desktop market. That said, Intel’s first attempt at a desktop chiplet-based competitor has not been well received, due to latency issues from the interconnect, which is responsible for connecting all the tiles together. Intel is attempting to rectify the issue through
firmware updates
. Still, its current implementation can’t touch AMD’s competing
Ryzen 9000
CPUs (such as the
9800X3D
), nor is it enough to even beat its own previous-generation 14th-generation processors in gaming (such as the
14900K
).

All that said, moving to a chiplet approach will afford Intel more ways to optimize its architectures down the road, in a more efficient manner. Each tile can be developed independently of others and built with different nodes to improve yields, optimize development, and reduce production costs.
