data.title: Sign in with Apple" broke after update–losing data for a third of users
data.author: gorniv
data.article_summary: Apple在2025年5月3日的维护期间，更改了“通过Apple登录”功能的用户识别机制，导致使用私有中继邮箱（@privaterelay.appleid.com）的用户无法收到邮件，且其userIdentifier被更改，使得系统无法识别原有账户。这一变化导致三分之一的用户失去访问权限，且无法通过邮件联系。开发者已向Apple发送三次支持请求，但未收到回复。文章提醒开发者不要仅依赖Apple登录，应实施备用方案，以防类似问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple ID系统的问题及其引发的用户访问和身份验证难题

不同观点：
• [lytefm] 认为Apple ID系统存在严重问题，基于其最近设置新MacBook时的糟糕体验，如无法创建账户、无法在App Store登录并输入支付信息等，最终通过查找非官方的解决方案才得以解决。
  
• [moi2388] 提到其平台使用了Apple的私人中继邮箱和一次性登录码作为替代方案，但有三分之一的用户因Apple ID问题而无法联系和恢复账户。他们建议可以通过临时允许一次性登录链接到其他邮箱来解决此问题，并关注Apple的回应。

• [ticulatedspline] 从技术角度分析，认为问题可能出在Apple ID与服务集成的过程中，涉及到用户标识符（userIdentifier）或OAUTH的sub claim改变，暗示这可能是技术实现上的问题。

• [zainhoda] 表示自己正要实现Apple登录功能，并对如果从头开始会如何做提出疑问，暗示了对当前问题如何规避或改进的关注。

• [j45] 质疑Apple ID作为iOS商店强制使用的要求，认为强制用户使用特定身份提供者会带来单一故障点，且如果作为可选项会更为合理。

• [andrewmcwatters] 强调不掌控自有技术会导致严重问题，建议使用Argon2id或scrypt等技术来增强安全性，暗示对外部身份验证系统的依赖会带来风险。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Apple ID系统的不稳定性和强制性要求，特别是对用户账户恢复和访问的影响。
• 讨论中涉及的技术问题，如私人中继邮箱、用户标识符变化等，显示出用户和开发者对Apple ID技术细节的困惑和不满。
• 对于如何改进，有人建议临时技术解决方案，也有人从根本上质疑强制使用Apple ID的必要性，并提倡开发者掌控自有技术以避免类似问题。

43905697.article_content:
Apple Sign In - Apple has removed private relay emails
Important
: If your ASO.dev profile contains a private email like
@privaterelay.appleid.com
, please contact
[email protected]
to update your address in our database.
Apple has removed all private relay emails associated with our service for users who signed in using Apple ID (this is an issue on Apple’s side that we cannot fix). As a result, we are currently unable to send you any emails, including informational messages and login code emails.
This issue began during Apple’s scheduled maintenance on May 3, 2025.
More details
On May 3, 2025, we faced a critical issue: “Sign in with Apple” stopped working properly for all users, resulting in the complete loss of access for one-third of our users—specifically, those using Apple’s private relay emails.
What exactly happened?
• Apple began returning a completely new userIdentifier for existing Apple IDs, without users initiating any changes. This effectively made user authentication impossible, as we can no longer match users to their existing data.
• The email field now always returns
null
. Although this behavior is typical for subsequent sign-ins, it’s irrelevant in this case because the userIdentifier itself changed, leaving no way to identify existing accounts.
• Previously issued relay emails (
@privaterelay.appleid.com
) no longer accept emails—we verified this with bounce tests.
• Users also report that our app has disappeared from their Apple ID’s authorized apps list.
Important context:
• We migrated our Apple Developer account from Individual to Organization about a year ago.
• Everything worked perfectly until the May 3, 2025 update.
• The incident occurred precisely on the day Apple released updates to the Developer Console (Accounts, Profiles, etc.). We strongly believe these internal changes at Apple triggered the issue.
Consequences:
• Every user received a new userIdentifier, meaning our system sees returning users as entirely new, breaking the link to their historical data.
• One-third of our users, who registered via Apple’s private relay email, are now completely unreachable:
• We can’t contact them (emails bounce).
• We can’t restore their access (new IDs don’t match old accounts).
• We have sent three support requests to Apple via email—no reply or acknowledgment yet, with no escalation path or live chat available.
⸻
🧠 We were fortunate because ASO.dev also supports an alternative sign-in method (email with a one-time login code). Without this alternative, we would’ve permanently lost access for every user who originally signed in with Apple.
⸻
We’re openly sharing this story to: • Warn developers who rely solely on Apple Sign-In and relay email addresses.
• Connect with others who’ve faced similar issues—let’s share experiences.
• Draw Apple’s attention to this critical problem—currently, there is no documented solution and no available support.
Never rely solely on Apple ID authentication. Always implement a fallback method, as even major ecosystems can fail unpredictably.
⸻

data.title: Cuttlefish 'talk' with their arms, study reveals
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 科学家发现乌贼通过独特的腕部动作进行交流，这些被称为“腕波信号”的动作包括“向上”、“侧面”、“翻滚”和“皇冠”四种姿态，每种姿态涉及不同的腕部位置和波动模式，常伴有体色变化。研究显示，这些信号可以通过视觉和水中振动被感知，形成多感官交流系统。乌贼对正放的视频信号反应更强烈，且能区分原始信号和被扰乱的信号。该发现揭示了乌贼复杂的交流方式，可能涉及侧线和平衡囊等感知水运动的器官，为进一步理解海洋无脊椎动物的交流提供了新视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同评论者对头足类动物（如鱿鱼、墨鱼、章鱼）以及其他生物的智力、感知能力和沟通方式的讨论。

不同观点：
• [A_D_E_P_T] 认为鱿鱼不值一提，但人们应该停止食用墨鱼和大章鱼，因为它们表现出高度的智力和好玩性。
• [CommenterPerson] 表示因为鱼类、鸡、牛、山羊等生物都是有感知能力的，所以自己选择了素食。

• [enneff] 通过个人经验分享，提到自己潜水时和墨鱼有过长时间的眼神交流，感觉墨鱼有复杂的思维活动。

• 一些评论者（如 [A_D_E_P_T] 和 [CommenterPerson]）关注生物的感知能力和智力，并基于此提出是否应改变人类对待这些生物的态度（如停止食用）。
• 其他评论者（如 [go_elmo] 和 [damnitbuilds]）则更广泛地讨论了不同生物之间的沟通方式，并对“交流”的定义提出质疑和思考。

43904478.article_content:
ig. 1. Four distinct arm wave signs observed in adult Sepia officinalis (A–D) and juvenile Sepia bandensis (E–H):
“Up” sign (A, E): The most frequently displayed gesture, characterized by upward extension of the first arm pair and outward extension of the fourth pair, while the second and third arm pairs are twisted at the midsection.
“Side” sign (B, F): All arms are rolled to one side of the body, creating a lateral display.
“Roll” sign (C, G): All arms are tucked and rolled beneath the head, altering its shape to highlight the eyes.
“Crown” sign (D, H): Features a rapid “spitting” motion, with arms arranged in a crown-like formation.
Scientists have discovered that cuttlefish use distinct arm movements to communicate with each other, adding another dimension to these already remarkable marine creatures.
Researchers from the École Normale Supérieure in Paris and the Italian Institute of Technology have identified specific arm gestures they’ve named “arm wave signs” that appear to serve as a communication system between cuttlefish. The study, published this month in bioRxiv, reveals that these underwater signals can be perceived both visually and through water vibrations – essentially creating a multi-sensory conversation.
According to the researchers, this newly discovered behavior involves distinct arm movements that follow specific patterns in two cuttlefish species. These arm wave signs involve deliberate, expressive arm undulations that can last several seconds and be combined in various sequences.
The research team, led by Sophie Cohen-Bodénès and Peter Neri, documented these movements over months of observation. They identified four distinct gestures they named “up,” “side,” “roll,” and “crown” signs. Each movement involves different arm positions and undulating motions, often combined with color changes on the cuttlefish’s skin.
What makes this discovery particularly intriguing is that the cuttlefish responded differently to these signals depending on their orientation. When shown videos of other cuttlefish performing these arm waves, the animals were significantly more likely to “wave back” when the video was displayed right-side up versus upside-down – similar to how humans perceive faces and other socially relevant displays.
But perhaps most surprisingly, the researchers found evidence that these arm motions might be perceived not just visually but also through vibrations in the water. Using specially designed playback experiments, they recorded the mechanical waves produced by these arm movements and played them back to test subjects.
The researchers found that these signals work through multiple sensory channels. By using specialized playback experiments, they demonstrated that cuttlefish can perceive these communications both visually and through water movement detection.
The cuttlefish were more responsive to the original recordings compared to versions that were played backward or scrambled – suggesting they could detect meaningful information in these water movements.
This dual-channel communication system might utilize the cuttlefish’s lateral line and statocysts, sensory organs that detect water movement and low-frequency vibrations. These findings suggest an intriguing parallel between cephalopod communication and the audiovisual communication seen in vertebrates – despite evolving independently.
The team points to fascinating evolutionary parallels, suggesting that just as cephalopods independently evolved camera-like eyes similar to vertebrates, their sensory systems for detecting water movement may have evolved to serve communication functions similar to vertebrate hearing.
The exact meaning behind these arm signs remains unclear. The researchers observed them in various contexts – during mating, hunting, defensive situations, and sometimes spontaneously. This suggests the signs might serve multiple purposes depending on the situation.
The discovery opens new avenues for understanding communication in marine invertebrates and adds to our appreciation of cephalopod intelligence. These surprisingly sophisticated “conversations” taking place beneath the waves highlight how much we still have to learn about communication in the animal kingdom.
Looking ahead, the research team hopes to explore how this discovery might provide insights into communication between vastly different animal species, potentially opening new pathways for understanding how diverse creatures interact with their environment.

data.title: Internet usage pattern during power outage in Spain and Portugal
data.author: ghoshbinayak
data.article_summary: 本文回顾了2025年4月28日伊比利亚半岛大停电期间的网络流量变化。作者分析了西班牙和葡萄牙在停电前后的流量数据，发现这两个国家在停电期间的网络流量显著下降。停电始于葡萄牙时间11:33，影响持续到次日凌晨。尽管桌面设备流量锐减80%，移动设备流量仅下降40%，表明人们更多依赖移动网络。停电期间，葡萄牙的移动网络使用量增加了30%，而有线连接（如WiFi）则大幅下降。人们主要访问新闻和政府网站，以获取停电相关信息，同时对食品安全网站的访问量也增加，反映出公众对食物保存的关注。西班牙的流量模式类似，但恢复较慢。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：西班牙大面积停电期间的互联网连接、通信状况以及应对措施

不同观点：
• **codetrotter** 提到在停电期间，移动互联网非常不稳定，无法有效获取信息，且由于依赖电子支付，停电带来生活上的不便。他通过太阳能充电设备尝试解决电力问题，最终通过外出散步和去海滩打发了时间。
• **TrianguloY** 表示在大学里由于备用发电机，有线网络较快恢复，而家中的路由器则大多停止工作。移动网络拥堵是主要问题，大学内由于人少，网络体验较好。
• **giorgioz** 分享了自己的经历，称自己的3G数据连接维持了较长时间，且通过电池供电的纤维连接也保持了4小时。他指出不同运营商的信号表现可能不同。
• **wkat4242** 强调互联网几乎无法使用，即使是5G网络也完全不可用，大多数人只能在极少数时段内获得有限的数据连接。他提到使用Iridium作为应急通信手段。
• **whitehexagon** 提到电力和移动服务恢复的时间差，银行和ATM的离线导致人们无法获取现金，初期信息匮乏引发了恐慌。
• **anthk** 分享了自己使用低带宽代理访问新闻网站的经验，并提到一些人购买了FM收音机以应对紧急情况。他还反驳了关于西班牙午休的误解。
• **dukeofdoom** 提到多年前在安大略类似的停电经历，认为这种经历让人们更多地进行户外交流，并表达了对无现代技术生活的向往。

补充讨论：
• **dagi3d** 和 **Funes-** 对关于西班牙午餐时间和午休的描述提出了批评，认为这种描述不准确且有误导性。
• **myself248** 和 **NooneAtAll3** 对手机电池电量信息泄露到互联网的问题提出了质疑。
• **onionisafruit** 对政府食品安全网站的低访问量表示惊讶。
• **sillyfluke** 对西班牙和葡萄牙人在欧盟其他地区使用本地手机的体验差异表示好奇，特别是关于漫游服务的影响。

争议焦点：
• 关于西班牙午餐时间和午休的描述不准确，引发了对文化误解的争论。
• 不同用户在停电期间对移动网络体验的描述存在差异，可能与运营商和所在位置有关。

43894363.article_content:
A look back at the Iberian power outage of April 28
By
Philip Tellis
on
03 May 2025
Table of Contents
Overall traffic
Identifying the Anomaly
Drilling into the details
How long could it last?
In closing
On Monday, April 28, the
Iberian Peninsula suffered a major power outage
that
disabled many services
across these countries.  In this post I'll look at the patterns we saw in
mPulse data during this time.
Overall traffic
I first looked at the overall data patterns for traffic originating from Spain & Portugal for several weeks prior to the outage.
While
other regions
were also
slightly affected
, these two countries
suffered the worst of it.
The image above shows traffic patterns for these two countries for 7 days around the event at 1 hour granularity. We see that on average (in that mode I mean the medians),
Spain has about 4.5 times the traffic of Portugal. This is expected, since Spain's population (48m) is 4.5 times that of Portugal (10.5).
Identifying the Anomaly
I then ran mPulse's Anomaly Detection against this data.
The Anomaly Detection logic shows that traffic dropped below expected levels between 12pm & 1pm
CEST
(local time in Madrid),
and then returned to normal sometime around 2am on the 29th.  This chart only shows traffic from Spain, but you get the picture.
Drilling into the details
I then looked at the data at finer granularity. This time at 5 minute intervals comparing April 28th to the week prior. Ideally I'd have used the previous Monday, but as that
was the Easter Monday holiday, the traffic patterns were unusual on that day as well. I settled on Wednesday, April 23rd as a representative day for the prior week. Just to be
sure, I also looked at data from France & Germany to make sure we weren't seeing a common change in pattern.
Also, to be clear, for any of the following charts that refer to a single country, the time axis will be in that country's time zone. This means that Portugal shows up in
WEST
rather than
CEST
.
The outage started at 11:33am in Portugal which is 12:33pm in Spain.
I looked at several different dimensions, but the first one to stand out was Device Type.
Mobile Lunches
For all 4 countries that I looked at, there is a sharp drop in desktop traffic around lunch time. In France and Portugal desktop traffic drops from about 12-2pm with its trough
around 1pm.  In Germany the drop is between 12-1pm while in Spain it starts around 1pm, and goes until 4 or 5pm. The drop in Spain is less steep than that in France & Portugal
suggesting that it's more staggerred across this 3-4 hour period rather than all at once.
During this afternoon break, we see traffic moving to mobile devices.
During the outage
At the start of the power outage, we notice that while traffic drops 80% on desktop, there is only a 40% drop on mobile. At this time, and going on for a few hours,
there is more mobile traffic than desktop traffic. In fact mobile traffic remains higher than desktop traffic until the next morning, but this appears to be a common
pattern where traffic typically moves to mobile as people leave work around 5pm.
I was curious about that intial part of the outage. If there wasn't power, then how were people still connecting to the Internet? Naturally their phones still had sufficient
battery power, but were there cell phone signals or other networks that were usable?
Connection sources
For these charts I looked only at mobile devices to see how they were connecting to the Internet.
For both Spain & Portugal, we see that Wired connections (this includes WiFi you may have at home, the office or a coffee shop since it uses
NAT
over a wire, but not ISP provided WiFi networks where you get a public IP over WiFi) drop off significantly. There's about a 50 percentage point drop in wired traffic. At
the same time, Portugal saw a 30 percentage point increase in Cellular network usage. There were even a few wireless hotspots that appear at this time.
Destinations
What kinds of sites were most interesting at this time? What were people willing to use their limited electric reserves on? I grouped destination sites by Industry to
try and make some sense of it.
There are different patterns for Spain & Portugal, so I'll look at them separately.
Remember that in Portugal the outage started at 11:33am local time. Almost immediately we see an
increase
in traffic to news websites with people trying to find out
what was going on. There are also periodic updates on government websites that see an increase in traffic.
There's a drop in Retail, Entertainment and Financial activity.
There is also a sudden new stream of visits to sites dealing with Food Safety and the safe handling of food, possibly because people have to figure out what's safe to hold
on to without refrigeration.  I should mention that there were no visits to these sites at any time prior to this event for the several weeks that I looked at the data.
Food safety and Government websites seem to be common with Spain as well.
However Spanish us

data.title: Game Bub: open-source FPGA emulation handheld
data.author: truxs
data.article_summary: Game Bub是一款即将推出的开源FPGA复古模拟手持游戏设备，支持Game Boy、Game Boy Color和Game Boy Advance游戏。它可以通过插入原始游戏卡带或从microSD卡加载ROM文件进行游戏，并具备震动、实时时钟、加速计和陀螺仪等功能，确保兼容大部分游戏。设备采用AMD Artix™ 7 FPGA，拥有3.5英寸IPS屏幕、立体声扬声器和USB Type-C充电接口，电池续航超过15小时。Game Bub还支持多人游戏链接和可选的Game Bub Dock，可通过HDMI连接电视并支持蓝牙控制器。所有硬件和软件均为开源，用户可以自由开发和修改。

is an open-source FPGA-based retro emulation handheld that supports Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance games.
Game Bub can play original game cartridges, as well as ROM files loaded from a microSD card. When emulating a cartridge, Game Bub has built-in rumble, real-time clock, accelerometer, and gyroscope, so most games, no matter how unique, will work the way you expect. Game Bub also supports link cables for multiplayer gaming with other Game Bub devices or original Game Boy and Game Boy Advance systems.
Play It Again
Game Bub is the first fully open-source FPGA retro-emulation handheld. Game Bub plays your collection of physical Game Boy and Game Boy Advance cartridges, and you can also enjoy the thriving Game Boy homebrew and romhack scene by loading ROMs you own from a microSD card—no flashcart needed. Game Bub also includes built-in cartridge backup and restore functionality: never lose a save file again!
No matter how you load your games, you’ll benefit from ultra-low input latency and compatibility with a wide array of original accessories.
Game Bub modernizes the classic handheld experience with detailed stereo speakers and a vivid backlit IPS screen. You won’t need to hunt down AA batteries, either—Game Bub has 15+ hours of battery life and is rechargeable over USB Type-C.
But, Game Bub is more than just an FPGA-based handheld. It’s fully open source (hardware, firmware, and gateware) and fully hackable, so you can use it as a portable, self-contained AMD Artix™ 7 FPGA development platform—with unrestricted access to all on-board hardware. With Game Bub, batteries
are
included (literally and figuratively): develop your own FPGA game cores, or use it to build other interactive FPGA experiences with its suite of I/O, peripherals, and features.
Game on the Big Screen
The
Game Bub Dock
is a separate accessory that allows Game Bub handhelds to connect to a TV or monitor using its HDMI port.
The Dock also adds Bluetooth controller support: it’s compatible with Xbox, DualShock/DualSense, Switch Pro, 8BitDo, and many more controllers!
Features & Specifications
Classic System Compatibility
Game Boy-compatible cartridge slot for Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance games
Custom FPGA cores designed for high accuracy and physical hardware compatibility
Built-in ROM loading and backup
GBA-type multiplayer link port (also compatible with Game Boy Color)
Rumble motor for games with force feedback
Accelerometer and gyroscope for compatible games
Real-time clock
Modern System Specs
FPGA
: Built around the powerful AMD Artix™ 7 XC7A100T FPGA, with 101,400 logic cells and 607.5 KiB of block RAM
MCU
: ESP32-S3 microcontroller for auxiliary tasks
Wireless
: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE
Memory
: 32 MiB of SDRAM and 512 KiB of SRAM connected to the FPGA
Display
: 3.5 inch 480 x 320 IPS LCD
Audio
: Stereo 1 W speakers, TRS headphone jack
Input
: 12 buttons for the FPGA, 4 additional system buttons for the MCU only
Expansion
: PMOD header
Storage
: microSD card slot
Power
: USB Type-C charging, 15+ hour in-game time
Optional Dock
: HDMI-out and wireless controller compatibility, simultaneous charging
Open Source
Game Bub is fully open source! All hardware, firmware, and gateware source files are available on the
GitHub repository
. The repository also has a detailed
architecture document
.

data.title: Towards the Cutest Neural Network
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
文章主要描述了作者尝试在微控制器上使用神经网络估算物体姿态的过程。由于传感器读数非线性且相互耦合，无法通过解析方法解决，作者决定训练一个简单的神经网络来近似逆映射函数，从传感器读数到姿态。作者通过在计算机上生成训练数据，训练了一个小型神经网络，并计划将其部署在Cortex-M0微控制器上进行推理。

作者遇到了几个挑战，包括微控制器不支持浮点运算，需要整数量化。经过研究，作者使用TensorFlow进行量化感知训练，并采用Rust的microflow-rs库进行推理。然而，microflow-rs和TensorFlow的量化例程仍依赖浮点运算，而作者希望实现仅使用整数运算的“最简洁”神经网络。

文章还简要介绍了神经网络的基本数学原理，包括输入数据、输出预测、权重、偏置和激活函数等概念。作者希望通过分享自己的经验，帮助其他有类似需求的人，并期待获得更简洁解决方案的建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在Cortex-M0和M3等嵌入式系统上实现神经网络的优化方法

不同观点：
• JanSchu认为可以通过预先计算固定点乘数和位移来完全去除M0上的浮点指令，并通过CMSIS-NN库使用int8内核实现快速计算。他强调了手工编写推理循环的重要性，并提供了一种从PyTorch原型到C代码的具体工作流程。
• gwern建议使用随机搜索或进化算法如CMA-ES来训练特定任务的神经网络，因为这些方法易于实现，且训练速度快。
• QuadmasterXLII支持JanSchu的方法，并分享了自己使用C++和Eigen进行推理的经验，认为直接实现推理方程的代码量远小于使用框架的配置文件。
• alexpotato推荐了一个简单的Python神经网络示例，认为这对初学者有帮助。
• mattdesl提出了BitNet（三值权重）在受限硬件上的潜力，并提供了相关文献和代码资源。
• jasonjmcghee询问了贝叶斯状态估计算法如无迹卡尔曼滤波器的考虑，认为这可能是一个可行的替代方案。
• gitroom对优化技巧在现实应用中的效果表示怀疑，认为需要实际验证。
• nico对文章内容做了轻松的评论，没有提出具体的技术观点。
• thomassmith65质疑了使用jax.nn的优势，认为从零开始编写小神经网络的例子很多。
• hansvm详细讨论了手写推理循环的优点，并指出了一些在嵌入式系统上优化神经网络性能的技巧，如数据对齐和列主存储。
• imtringued批评文章作者在没有特殊情况下选择了复杂的量化感知训练方法，认为这是不必要的，并推荐使用后训练静态量化方法。
• light_hue_1强烈批评文章的复杂性和缺乏系统性，建议初学者使用PyTorch实现简单网络，并逐步优化，而不是一开始就尝试自定义实现。

补充讨论：
• 关于使用3x3矩阵表示旋转和空间位置的问题，Onavo指出在机器人学/逆运动学应用中，使用3x3矩阵可以避免万向节锁问题。
• 讨论中多次提到CMSIS-NN库和PyTorch在嵌入式神经网络实现中的应用，显示了这两种工具在实际应用中的重要性。
• 关于量化方法的讨论，包括量化感知训练（QAT）和后训练静态量化（PTSQ），反映了不同方法在实际应用中的优缺点。

争议焦点：
• imtringued和light_hue_1对文章作者选择复杂的量化感知训练方法提出了强烈批评，认为这是不必要的，并推荐使用更简单和系统的方法。
• hansvm和JanSchu对如何优化嵌入式系统上的神经网络性能提出了不同的见解，特别是在固定点和浮点运算的选择上。

总结：
讨论主要围绕在嵌入式系统上实现神经网络的优化方法展开，涉及具体的实现技巧、量化方法的选择以及不同工具和算法的优缺点。参与者分享了各自的经验和建议，提供了多种技术路线和资源供参考。

43861297.article_content:
Towards the cutest neural network ← Back to Kevin's homepage Published: 2025 April 28 I recently needed to use a microcontroller to estimate the pose (translation and orientation) of an object using readings from six different sensors. Since the readings were non-linear and coupled with each other, an explicit analytical solution was out of the question. I figured I’d have a go at using a simple neural network to approximate it: generate training data (on my computer) using a forward simulation (pose to sensor readings) train a lil’ neural network (a few dense layers, 100’s of parameters, tops) to approximate the inverse mapping function (sensor readings to pose) deploy this network on my microcontroller (Cortex-M0, 16 kB RAM, 32 kB flash) to actually do the inference Since neural networks have been around since the 1980’s, I figured it’d be straightforward. A quick background search uncovered lots of promising leads too, especially regarding “quantization”, which I wanted to do as my microcontroller doesn’t have hardware support for floating point operations. However, this turned out to be much more difficult than I’d anticipated. It seems like my use case — end-to-end training of a simple dense neural network with integer-only inference — is quite uncommon. The vast majority of papers and software libraries I found turned out to be complex, heavyweight (in terms of inference code size), and have lots of unstated assumptions and background requirements. To make a web design analogy: It felt like I kept falling into npm create-react-app rabbit holes rather than what I wanted: The moral equivalent of opening index.html with notepad.exe and typing

Welcome to my Homepage

. I’m writing up my notes to: checkpoint my understanding of the space and current best solution help anyone else who simply wants a wholesome lil’ universal function approximator with low conceptual and hardware overhead solicit “why don’t you just …” emails from experienced practitioners who can point me to the library/tutorial I’ve been missing =D (see the alternatives-considered down the page for what I struck out on) tl;dr, how to do it? use TensorFlow to do quantization-aware training and save the resulting model out to a .tflite flatbuffer file use the microflow-rs crate for inference — it’s basically a proc macro that reads tflite file and generates straightforward Rust code that uses nalgebra to multiply matrices Props to Matteo for being seemingly the only person in this space who can put a clear “hello world” inference example in their README.md: use microflow :: model ; #[model( "path/to/model.tflite" )] struct MyModel ; fn main () { let prediction = MyModel :: predict ( input_data ); } It should be cuter. Unfortunately, MicroFlow (and TensorFlow’s out-of-the-box quantization routines, from what I can tell) require floating point operations for inference. While I could use software floating point, I want to make the cutest possible neural network, which means integer arithmetic operations only. (The code size and speed of software floating point depends on the routines used. qfplib-m0-full has a good overview and shows that, e.g., the GCC compiler software floating point multiplication takes 166 cycles.) On the MicroFlow side, removing floating point operations would require a big redesign, as: they’re baked into the API ( predict assumes f32 inputs and outputs). the internals themselves rely on floating point the MicroFlow proc macro reads the .tflite flatbuffer ( source ) when reading a fully-connected layer it combines the various quantization scale factors and zero points into f32 constants these constants are then used during inference at runtime On the TensorFlow side, I can’t find any documentation/options about whether the quantization-aware training routines use floating point activation scaling or if they can model quantized multipliers. But I’m getting ahead of myself — let’s first review the mathematics of neural networks and meaning of “quantization”. Neural network overview The basic idea of neural networks you have a bunch of training data: $x$, the input data you have (in my case, readings from six sensors) $y$, the output value you are trying to predict (the object pose) Since you have no idea how to go from $x$ to $y$ yourself, you throw together $n$ general equations (“layers”) like: \begin{align} a_1 &= \sigma(W_1 x + b_1) \newline a_2 &= \sigma(W_2 a_1 + b_2) \newline \vdots \newline \hat{y} &= \sigma(W_{n} a_{n-1} + b_n) \end{align} These equations take your input $x$ and make a prediction $\hat{y}$ which, hopefully, is close to $y$. The equations require: free parameters $W$ and $b$ (the “weights” and “biases”, respectively); in our case these are a matrix and vector rather than scalar values, since our input data $x$ comes from multiple sensors and the output pose $y$ has six components (three spatial positions and three spatial rotations) $\sigma$, some nonlinear “activation” function (traditionall

data.title: Oregon State University's Open Source Lab Is Running on Fumes
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 俄勒冈州立大学开源实验室（OSU OSL）面临资金短缺，缺少25万美元。该实验室成立于2003年，曾为Mozilla Firefox、Apache软件基金会、Linux基金会、Drupal等众多开源项目提供托管和基础设施支持。由于美国高等教育经费削减，实验室的未来面临威胁。实验室主任Lance Albertson表示，目前需要资金支持以维持运营。开源社区和曾受益于该实验室的项目纷纷表示支持，希望能够帮助其渡过难关。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OSU开源实验室（OSU Open Source Lab）的现状和变化

不同观点：
• mdaniel表示过去曾向OSU开源实验室捐款，但如今对其关注点产生疑惑，特别是对该组织似乎转向以PowerPC和aarch64为中心的关注。他引用了实验室的社区页面作为参考。

• voxadam提供了一个新闻链接，指出OSU开源实验室的未来可能面临危机，该新闻有102条评论，表明此事在社区内引起了广泛讨论。

• bgwalter将实验室的潜在问题归因于政治因素，具体提到反觉醒运动和特朗普计划，暗示俄勒冈在BLM抗议中的活跃表现可能影响了实验室的处境。他还提到GPL友好性可能与商业利益冲突，暗示开源社区中关于软件许可类型的争议。

• whalesalad分享了个人经历，提到在2005年时曾使用该实验室的镜像来安装Linux软件包，表明实验室在过去对开源社区有过实际贡献。

争议焦点：
• OSU开源实验室的技术方向转变及其背后的原因，特别是政治因素对技术决策的影响。

• 开源软件许可类型之间的争议，以及这些争议如何可能影响像OSU开源实验室这样的组织。

43904854.article_content:
Software
19
Oregon State University's Open Source Lab is running on fumes
19
Shakeup in US higher education funding means FOSS incubator is short a quarter of a million bucks
Liam Proven
Fri 2 May 2025
//
18:50 UTC
Higher education across the USA is facing federal funding cutbacks – and now the Oregon State University (OSU) Open Source Lab (OSL) is in trouble.
The boss of the
OSU
OSL
, Lance Albertson, reports a critical shortage of funding – putting the
future of the 22-year-old project
in jeopardy.
In the post, Albertson explained that OSL provides hosting for FOSS projects "from all over the world," listing "notable milestones over the years" as including:
Provided hosting for Mozilla Firefox when they needed help in the early days and hosted the release of 1.0
Was the home of the Apache Software Foundation, Linux Foundation, Kernel.org, Mozilla for many years
Offers fast and reliable software mirroring for projects
Currently provides infrastructure hosting for projects such as Drupal, Gentoo Linux, Debian, Fedora, phpBB, OpenID, Buildroot/Busybox, Inkscape, Cinc and many more!
Virtual machines for x86, aarch64 and ppc64le are used by many projects for CI and other hosted services
Not to be confused with the
University of Oregon
, OSU set up its Open Source Lab in 2003. Since then, it's done a great deal to help multiple FOSS projects. As
Linux.com reported in 2006
, it gave critical help to Gentoo and Drupal, along with providing one of the first hosting sites for the fledgling Mozilla Foundation.
As the
Drupal team reported
, the OSU OSL was serving 10 TB of data per month for them – in 2012. Seven years later,
LWN
reported on a
talk
by
Albertson
at
SCALE 17x
, saying that "role of the lab is to be a neutral hosting facility and to foster relationships between FOSS projects and companies."
KDE 3 lives to fight another day as Trinity Desktop 14.1.4 hits the shelves
Thunderbird joins Firefox on the monthly treadmill
BTW Windows Subsystem for Linux officially uses Arch now
OpenBSD 7.7 released with updated hardware support, 9Front ships second update of 2025
The OSL's site currently
lists 288 projects it supports
, though the page notes there may be more. The Gentoo project is already
soliciting help
for the OSL.
Over on the Hackernews message board, commenters were effusive about the org's impact, with one user
stating
: "The OSL was transformative for my career as a budding CS student in Corvallis many years ago. I can't say enough good things about the positive impact it has on the Open Source community and the students it employs."
Another commented: "When I was working on GHC many years ago, OSUOSL helped us by providing us access to some nice POWER7 machines (courtesy of an IBM kernel hacker who recommended and endorsed us) and we used them for years to solve weird issues. I've always thought very highly of the Open Source Lab. I hope someone can help them make it through this."
The Corvallis Gazette-Times, newspaper to the OSU hometown, recently reported on the impact of
the Trump administration's funding cuts
in its story, "
OSU raises tuition amid federal funding concerns
," and quoted from OSU President Jayathi Murthy's
report
to the university's board.
Murthy stated: "New federal priorities and proposed funding cuts, especially for research, may have direct, negative consequences for OSU."
Back in 2011, Facebook talked about its use of
OSU OSL test infrastructure
. The OSL reports that it is currently short $250,000, which we suspect Meta could readily find in pocket change. Whether it will is a different matter.
We've checked in with Albertson, who told us: "I have always loved
The Register
!" He declined to comment further, though indicated there may be more news from mid-May. ®

data.title: NASA budget proposal draws strong criticism – SpaceNews
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 白宫提议将NASA预算削减近25%并取消多个重大项目，包括终止月球 Gateway、太空发射系统（SLS）和猎户座（Orion）计划，以及火星样本返回任务等。这引发了国会议员和行业组织的强烈反对，认为这将严重影响美国的科学领导地位和太空探索能力。加拿大和欧洲的国际合作伙伴也对此表示担忧，尤其是欧洲航天局，因为其与NASA在火星探测等项目上有密切合作。尽管一些商业航天组织如商业空间联合会（CSF）对预算提案中的部分内容表示支持，但他们也批评了其他削减措施。整体而言，这一提案在美国国内外引发了广泛争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国太空计划的预算削减，特别是SLS（太空发射系统）和深空探测及天体物理学项目的资金变化。

不同观点：
• 观点一：支持取消SLS，认为商业航天部门可以承担部分发射任务。有人提到SLS的取消是积极的，暗示商业航天有能力替代部分传统航天项目，从而节省成本。[xqcgrek2]对这一观点可能持反对态度。

• 观点二：反对深空探测和天体物理学预算的大幅削减。这一观点认为，这类研究具有独特性和不可替代性，无法由商业公司完成。例如，[xqcgrek2]指出削减2/3的预算是非常不明智的，因为这些科学探索领域需要持续的资金支持和政府主导。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：预算削减是否合理，特别是深空探测和天体物理学项目。这些项目被认为具有科学价值和长期意义，无法简单由商业公司替代。

• 论据和例子：[xqcgrek2]提到深空探测和天体物理学的资金被削减了2/3，认为这是不明智的决策，因为这些研究领域具有高度的专业性和复杂性，商业部门难以胜任。这一论据强调了政府支持这些项目的重要性。

• 讨论关系：评论中隐含了对SLS取消的支持与对深空探测和天体物理学预算削减的反对之间的对比，显示出在预算调整中不同项目受到的不同影响及其引发的争议。

43903984.article_content:
Updated 6:55 p.m. Eastern with Canadian response.
WASHINGTON — The White House’s proposal to cut NASA’s budget by nearly 25% and cancel several major programs has drawn criticism from industry and members of Congress, while raising concerns among international partners.
The top-level or “skinny” budget released by the White House’s Office of Management and Budget May 2
proposed $18.8 billion for NASA in fiscal year 2026
, a $6 billion cut from the $24.9 billion the agency received in 2025. The budget called for the cancellation of the lunar Gateway, ending the Space Launch System and Orion programs after Artemis 3 and termination of science missions like Mars Sample Return. It also proposed curtailing use of the International Space Station and sharp cuts in space technology funding.
The proposal met with a strong negative reaction both on Capitol Hill and among space industry organizations. “Massive cuts to NASA in the President’s proposed budget are shocking – the largest in American history,” stated Rep. Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), ranking member of the House Appropriations Committee’s commerce, justice and science (CJS) subcommittee, whose jurisdiction includes NASA.
“They will decimate NASA’s research & education efforts and terminate funding for our nation’s dedicated scientists. Rather than rooting out so-called ‘government waste’, this budget puts American leadership in science, technology, & innovation at risk,” she said in a May 2
social media post
.

Her Senate counterpart, Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Committee’s CJS subcommittee, argued that the budget favored Elon Musk’s SpaceX. “We would never have gotten to the moon or be talking about Mars without NASA’s science mission — and should not let Trump/Musk jeopardize America’s future leadership,” he
stated
May 4.
Rep. George Whitesides (D-Calif.), vice ranking member of the House Science Committee, offered similar sentiments. “No spin will change the fact that this would end critical missions, dramatically scale back the workforce, and risk our scientific leadership around the globe,” he
said on social media
May 2. “It is completely irresponsible, and I will fight it every way I can.”
Industry groups representing both established and more entrepreneurial companies have criticized the budget proposal. The former is represented by the Coalition for Deep Space Exploration, whose members include Boeing, Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman, who have major contracts supporting SLS, Orion and Gateway that the budget proposal puts in jeopardy. The group also includes many smaller companies that are suppliers to those prime contractors.
In a May 2 statement, the group called the budget proposal “deeply concerning” to its members. “It threatens our scientific capabilities and jeopardizes a sustained human presence on the Moon, undermining U.S. leadership in space and making NASA’s exploration goals nearly impossible.”
“Diverting the attention, time, and resources away from existing capabilities opens the door to China, which is poised to take the lead on the lunar frontier with plans for crewed Moon landings by the end of the decade. It will endanger our current global leadership position in space,” the organization added.
The Commercial Space Federation (CSF), whose members include SpaceX, took a more nuanced view of the budget. “A thoughtful transition to more competitive commercial partnerships, as proposed by the ‘skinny budget’, will allow the U.S. to conduct human exploration programs with fewer resources,” it said in a May 5 statement.
However, the CSF criticized other elements of the budget proposal. “The proposed reductions to space and Earth science, space technology, and activity in low-Earth orbit and the ISS, impacting commercial utilization, will have significant negative consequences for the U.S. global posture and the commercial space economy,” it stated.
Also joining the criticism was The Planetary Society, which earlier spoke out about proposed deep cuts in NASA science. “Slashing NASA’s budget by this much, this quickly, without the input of a confirmed NASA Administrator or in response to a considered policy goal, won’t make the agency more efficient — it will cause chaos, waste the taxpayers’ investment, and undermine American leadership in space,” it said in a May 2 release.
European and Canadian concerns
Concerns about the NASA budget proposal extend beyond the United States. The European Space Agency would be significantly affected if the proposed budget was enacted, given its cooperation with NASA on Mars Samp

data.title: Grafana K6 v1.0.0
data.author: tbobm
data.article_summary:
Grafana k6 v1.0 发布，标志着项目在稳定性、支持和透明度方面的重大里程碑。此版本引入了多项新特性，包括：

1. **稳定性**：采用语义化版本控制，提供两年支持，并明确公共API。
2. **TypeScript支持**：无需转译，直接运行 `.ts` 脚本，支持类型安全。
3. **简化的扩展**：无需 `xk6` 工具链，扩展可直接使用。
4. **改进的测试总结**：分层结果输出，增强的阈值和检查，多种摘要模式。
5. **质量提升**：稳定模块如 `k6/browser`，改进的Grafana Cloud集成。

此版本凝聚了社区的巨大贡献，感谢所有参与者。

Grafana k6 v1.0 is here! 🎉
After 9 years of iteration and countless community contributions, we're thrilled to announce
Grafana k6 v1.0
.
While many features and capabilities in this release were introduced gradually in previous versions,
k6 v1.0 marks a turning point
: a commitment to stability, formal support guarantees, and transparency in how we evolve and develop the project from here. This milestone is more than a version number; it's about trust, reliability, and empowering you to test confidently.
Thank you, k6 community! 🌍
This release wouldn't be possible without you:
⭐️ 27000+ GitHub stars.
🧠 9000+ git commits.
🤝 200+ contributors.
🔁 Countless test runs of any scale, in every timezone.
It's been amazing to watch k6 grow from a simple load testing command-line tool into a comprehensive reliability tool, used by teams worldwide and supported by a passionate and dedicated community.
To everyone who filed bugs, built extensions and libraries, or championed k6:️
Thank you!
You've shaped what k6 is today. 🙇‍♂️
What's New in k6 1.0?
1. Stability You Can Build On
✅
Semantic Versioning
: k6 now follows
Semantic Versioning 2.0
. Breaking changes will only happen in major releases, with prior deprecation warnings.
🔒
2-Year Support Guarantees
: Every major version will be supported with critical fixes for
at least two years
; upgrade on your schedule.
📦
Public API Surface
: We've established a clearly delineated and supported API surface for the k6 codebase. Extensions, integrations, and projects building on top of the k6 code now have a stable foundation to rely on.
🔎 Read more in our
versioning and stability guarantees
guide.
2. First-Class TypeScript Support
Write type-safe and maintainable tests—no transpilation needed. Simply save your file with a
.ts
extension and run it directly using
k6 run script.ts
.

3. Extensions Made Simple
With k6 v1.0, extensions now work out of the box in
k6 cloud run
and
k6 cloud run --local-execution
. Support for
k6 run
is coming soon.
✅ No more xk6 toolchain.

To try the experimental feature, first enable its feature flag, then run it on Grafana Cloud with the following command:
K6_BINARY_PROVISIONING=true k6 cloud run script.js,
or if you want to run it locally and stream the results to Grafana Cloud then use:
K6_BINARY_PROVISIONING=true k6 cloud run --local-execution script.js
4. Revamped test summary
The new end-of-test summary makes it easier to
understand results and spot issues
:

Hierarchical output
: Metrics are grouped by scenario, group, and category.

Improved thresholds & checks
: Clearer layout for faster debugging.

:

(default): big picture results, focusing on essentials.

: full picture results, providing granularity.

,

data.title: Matt Godbolt sold me on Rust by showing me C++
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary:
本文由Gustavo Noronha撰写，介绍了Matt Godbolt通过C++演示让他认识到Rust的优点。文章首先赞扬了Matt在Compiler Explorer上的工作，并特别提到他的演讲《Correct by Construction: APIs That Are Easy to Use and Hard to Misuse》。作者有超过20年的C/C++经验，对演讲中提到的问题深有共鸣。

Matt在演讲中展示了一个发送股票订单的函数，指出C++中容易混淆参数类型的问题，比如用`double`表示价格和用`int`表示数量，编译器不会报错。作者尝试通过类型别名、类和显式构造函数来改进，但仍无法完全避免错误。最终，通过使用模板和静态断言，作者成功让编译器在参数错误时发出警告。

文章旨在展示Rust在类型安全方面的优势，并通过具体代码示例说明如何在C++中实现类似的保护机制。最终，通过复杂的代码改进，作者实现了编译时的类型检查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust与C++的比较，特别是在错误处理、类型安全、语言特性及库支持方面的差异。

不同观点：
• **Rust的错误处理优于C++**：[dvratil]认为Rust通过`Result`类型和`?`操作符使得错误处理更加一致和简便，而C++中存在多种错误处理方式，缺乏一致性，即使是标准库也是如此。
• **C++也能实现类似Rust的模式**：[thrwyexecbrain]指出，现代C++可以通过良好的设计模式（如明确的类型和生命周期管理）实现与Rust类似的代码风格，区别主要在于构建系统和编译器提示的差异。
• **Rust的防御性编程未必有效**：[antirez]认为，Rust提倡的防御性编程（如强类型）未必能提高代码质量，代码质量更多依赖于严格的测试和质量控制。
• **库的支持是关键**：[kasajian]认为，C++也能通过合适的库实现Rust的特性，因此问题不在于语言本身，而在于可用的库。
• **语言特性和库特性需区分**：[jpc0]提醒不要将语言特性和库特性混为一谈，并指出C++的隐式转换是导致一些问题的原因，而Rust没有这种问题。
• **C++有工具可以改善类型转换问题**：[grumbel]提到，C++中可以使用`-Wconversion`来捕获一些类型转换问题，但并不能解决所有情况。
• **Rust缺乏关键字参数是缺点**：[GardenLetter27]和[jsat]都提到，Rust缺乏命名参数或关键字参数，导致需要更多的样板代码。
• **简化C语言的设想**：[markus_zhang]提出，是否可以创建一种去除 quirks 的C语言变种，使其更安全但不增加复杂性。
• **Rust的内存安全优势**：[tumdum_]表示，Rust最吸引人的地方在于消除了由于内存损坏导致的Heisenbugs。

补充讨论：
• **对atoi的批评**：多个评论（如[dvratil], [writebetterc]）提到，在现代C++中不应使用`atoi`，而应使用STL中的转换函数以获得更好的错误处理。
• **Rust的学习曲线和社区资源**：[morning-coffee]提到，通过学习《Rust Book》转向了Rust，而[favorited]则提到一个与Rust相关的播客，提供了更多学习资源。

争议焦点：
• **强类型和防御性编程的价值**：一些开发者（如[antirez]）认为Rust的强类型和防御性编程未必能带来实际价值，而另一些开发者（如[dvratil], [jpc0]）则认为这些特性显著提高了代码的可靠性。
• **命名参数的必要性**：部分开发者（如[GardenLetter27], [jsat]）认为Rust缺乏命名参数是一个显著缺点，而其他开发者则未提及此问题，显示出对语言特性需求的个体差异。

data.title: Show HN: Feedsmith — Fast parser & generator for RSS, Atom, OPML feed namespaces
data.author: macieklamberski
data.article_summary: Feedsmith 是一个强大且快速的 JavaScript 解析和生成工具，支持 RSS、Atom、JSON Feed 和 RDF  feeds，同时支持 Podcast、iTunes、Dublin Core 和 OPML 文件。它提供通用和特定格式的解析器，保持原始 feed 结构，并智能规范化旧版元素。其特点包括对大小写不敏感、高性能、类型安全、树形抖动、良好的跨平台兼容性及全面的测试。支持多种格式和命名空间的解析与生成，如 Atom、Dublin Core、Syndication、Content、iTunes 等。安装通过 npm 进行，使用简便，提供通用和专用解析函数，返回对象包含所有支持的命名空间数据。

Feedsmith
Robust and fast JavaScript parser and generator for RSS, Atom, JSON Feed, and RDF feeds, with support for popular namespaces and OPML files. It provides both universal and format-specific parsers that maintain the original feed structure while offering helpful normalization.
Feedsmith maintains the original feed structure in a clean, object-oriented format. It intelligently normalizes legacy elements, providing you with complete access to all feed data without compromising simplicity.

• [renegat0x0] 对项目表示赞赏，但认为多次实现RSS阅读器是无意义的，因此开发了自己的API形式的RSS阅读器（crawler-buddy）。该工具专注于爬取功能，通过JSON API简化使用，避免了传统请求和浏览器操作。提到使用python的feedparser时遇到的一些XML解析问题，因此选择自行开发简化版。

• [urbanisierung] 简单地对项目表示赞赏，没有提出具体的技术讨论或问题。

• [piotrkulpinski] 关注性能问题，询问是否有与类似包的性能对比基准测试，显示出对工具效率和实用性的关注。

• [vivzkestrel] 比较了python的feedparser和该库（feedsmith），询问两者之间的区别和优劣，显示出对技术选型的关注，特别是两种工具在实际使用中的差异。

补充讨论：
• [renegat0x0] 提供的crawler-buddy工具自动检测网站的RSS源并进行爬取，专注于核心元素如缩略图，舍弃了一些RSS的细节功能，表明其工具设计上更偏向于特定用途（如爬取和简化处理）。

• [piotrkulpinski] 和 [vivzkestrel] 都提出了对性能和功能的对比需求，显示出社区对RSS工具在不同场景下的性能表现和功能细节的关注。

争议焦点：
• 不同RSS工具之间的功能和性能对比，特别是feedparser和feedsmith之间的差异，以及是否需要多次实现类似的RSS阅读器功能。

data.author: kevinlinxc

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能眼镜在音乐乐谱显示中的应用及其技术实现

不同观点：
• Aidevah认为Lilypond是一个优秀的乐谱排版工具，能够实现可缩放的乐谱显示，但可能难以在智能眼镜上运行。他指出了Lilypond在乐谱排版中的优势，同时也提到了在智能眼镜上应用的困难。

• eitally建议与大型数字乐谱供应商（如Musescore或Music Notes）合作或出售技术。他认为这对于钢琴演奏者是一个有吸引力的应用场景，并提出了集成节拍器和DAW控制等功能的需求。

• mdp2021对项目中使用的硬件和软件选择提出质疑，认为Epson Moverio AR眼镜在规格和价格上都更具优势，且软件架构过于复杂，缺乏竞争力。

• pedalpete分享了个人使用场景，强调了在演奏时无需手动操作的便利性，并建议增加自动滚动和节拍器功能，以提升用户体验。

• floren担心当前的系统显示速度是否足够，指出三秒发送位图可能导致乐谱显示跟不上快速演奏的速度。

• KyleBrandt幽默地提到如果智能眼镜看起来像普通眼镜或时尚墨镜，乐队在舞台上不用乐谱架会更美观。

• analog31指出在某些音乐 genre 中，乐谱通常以PDF形式存在，因此能够适应纸质乐谱的功能会非常有用。

• zharknado简单地对视频和项目表示赞赏。

• theyknowitsxmas幽默地建议给指挥一个按钮代替30个踏板。

• paul7986讨论了Meta Ray Bans智能眼镜的实用性和局限性，认为它们是手机的补充而不是替代品，并对其未来发展持怀疑态度。

• MarcelOlsz简单地表示这对视奏非常有帮助。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是项目中使用的AR眼镜和软件架构的合理性。mdp2021认为有更好的选择，而Aidevah则关注技术实现的难度。
• 用户对智能眼镜的实际应用场景有不同看法，eitally和pedalpete强调了其在音乐演奏中的潜在价值，而paul7986则对其在更广泛市场中的接受度持怀疑态度。
• 功能需求方面，eitally和pedalpete提出了集成节拍器、DAW控制和自动滚动等功能的需求，这些功能可以提升用户体验并增加产品的吸引力。

data.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Google发布了Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview版，重点增强了编码性能，特别是在前端和UI开发方面。新版本在WebDev Arena排行榜上排名第一，显示了其在构建美观且实用的网页应用方面的优势。它还提升了视频理解能力，支持从视频生成代码，并在Google AI Studio中推出了“Video to Learning App”功能。此外，Gemini 2.5 Pro在功能开发和应用概念实现上更加高效，能够帮助开发者快速将想法转化为实际应用。更新版本已经可以在Google AI Studio和Vertex AI中使用，且无需额外操作即可享受性能提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gemini 2.5 模型的表现及使用体验

不同观点：
• segphault 认为Gemini 2.5 模型在编程中比其他模型更少出现虚构API的情况，能替代搜索和StackOverflow进行日常编程，但仍无法像人类一样处理抽象和架构问题。
• paulirish 指出Gemini 2.5 Pro 在WebDev Arena排行榜上名列前茅，但该平台的系统提示仅支持React和Tailwind技术，对其他框架如 vanilla JS 支持不佳，并担忧这种狭隘的定义对模型竞争的影响。
• ranyume 抱怨Gemini 2.5 生成的代码包含过多注释，显得过于冗余。
• andy12_ 提到在某些基准测试中，Gemini 2.5 的新版本在多数项目上得分略低于旧版本，但在LiveCodeBench上表现更优。
• mohsen1 对比Gemini 2.5 和o3-mini的基准测试结果，指出Gemini在多个已知基准上仍落后于o3。
• laborcontract 认为Gemini 2.5 在基于diff的代码编辑上表现出色，但在生成完全匹配的diff上仍有不足，并关注模型的更新和免费层的可用性。
• herpdyderp 觉得Gemini 的UI体验差，建议通过技术手段提取输出内容。
• ionwake 询问如何在Cursor中使用Gemini 2.5 模型，并对模型的支持情况表示关注。
• killerstorm 建议使用版本号代替“新预览”这样的命名方式，以避免混淆。
• arnaudsm 指出Gemini 2.5 在多个基准测试中表现不如03-25版本，并怀疑是由于训练过程中的问题。
• m_kos 列举了在Gemini Advanced中使用2.5 Pro时遇到的一系列技术问题和bug。
• siwakotisaurav 对Gemini 在WebDev Arena上的表现表示惊讶，认为Claude在此领域长期领先。
• mliker 对Gemini 的“视频到学习应用”功能表示赞赏，认为其在教育领域有发展潜力。
• childintime 关注Gemini 在Python和JavaScript之外的语言（如C#和Zig）上的表现，并提到Ctrl+C无法正常工作的问题。
• djrj477dhsnv 表示在自己的工作中，Grok的表现优于Gemini，对Gemini被普遍认为更好的观点感到不解。

补充讨论：
• Gemini 2.5 模型的代码生成注释过多问题引起关注。
• WebDev Arena 平台的技术限制和对模型竞争的影响被讨论。
• Gemini 2.5 模型在不同编程语言上的表现和兼容性问题被提及。
• 用户对Gemini 2.5 模型的版本命名和更新策略提出改进建议。
• 技术支持和UI体验问题被认为是影响用户体验的重要因素。

争议焦点：
• Gemini 2.5 模型在不同基准测试中的表现是否优于其他模型存在不同看法。
• WebDev Arena 的技术限制是否影响了Gemini 2.5 模型的实际应用价值。
• 用户在实际工作中对Gemini 和Grok 模型的表现评价不一，存在争议。

Gemini
Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview: even better coding performance
MAY 6, 2025
Logan Kilpatrick
Senior Product Manager
Gemini API and Google AI Studio
Share
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Mail
We’ve seen developers doing amazing things with
Gemini 2.5 Pro
, so we decided to release an updated version a couple of weeks early to get into developers hands sooner.
Today we’re excited to release Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview (I/O edition). This update features even stronger coding capabilities, for you to start building with before Google I/O later this month. Expect meaningful improvements for front-end and UI development, alongside improvements in fundamental coding tasks such as transforming and editing code, and creating sophisticated agentic workflows.
“We found Gemini 2.5 Pro to be the best frontier model when it comes to "capability over latency" ratio. I look forward to rolling it out on Replit Agent whenever a latency-sensitive task needs to be accomplished with a high degree of reliability.”
–
Michele Catasta, President,
Replit
Best-in-class frontend web development
Gemini 2.5 Pro now ranks #1 on the
WebDev Arena leaderboard
, which measures human preference for a model’s ability to build aesthetically pleasing and functional web apps. Drawing on this leading capability, Gemini 2.5 Pro powers Cursor’s innovative code agent and empowers our collaborations with companies like Cognition and Replit. Together, we're pushing the frontiers of agentic programming to unlock new possibilities for developers.
“The updated Gemini 2.5 Pro achieves leading performance on our junior-dev evals. It was the first-ever model that solved one of our evals involving a larger refactor of a request routing backend. It felt like a more senior developer because it was able to make correct judgement calls and choose good abstractions.”
–
Silas Alberti, Founding Team,
Cognition
Gemini 2.5 Pro in action
Gemini 2.5 Pro’s deep understanding of code, combined with powerful reasoning, continues to make Gemini 2.5 Pro the go-to model for developers. We’re particularly excited about how this model can be used in the following cases.
Video to code
Gemini 2.5 Pro delivers state-of-the-art video understanding, scoring 84.8% on the VideoMME benchmark. Combining this with coding enables new flows that were previously not possible with previous versions. For example, the
Video to Learning App
in Google AI Studio demonstrates how Gemini 2.5 Pro creates an interactive learning app based on a single YouTube video. With improved video understanding and complete UI, the updated Gemini 2.5 Pro model delivers a more functional experience than the previous simple example.
Link to Youtube Video
(visible only when JS is disabled)
Easier feature development
Gemini 2.5 Pro is strong at front-end web development, helping you get more done. Implementing new features means manually diving into design files and inspecting components to match style properties like colors, fonts, padding, margins, and borders then manually writing the CSS code needed to replicate those visual properties accurately. Now imagine using Gemini 2.5 Pro in an IDE and having the model generate new features, like adding a video player in the style of the other apps in the
Gemini 95
starter app.
Link to Youtube Video
(visible only when JS is disabled)
Quick concepts to working apps
Bringing ideas to life with both functionality and a beautiful UI is made easier with Gemini 2.5 Pro. The new
dictation starter app
, built using the updated model, is a great example of this in action. Pay attention to some of the details like the wavelength animations, responsive design, and subtle button hover effects. By default, the model has a real taste for aesthetic web development while maintaining its steerability, helping developers quickly take a concept to a working web app. Gemini 2.5 Pro was able to design and code the microphone UI animation for the dictation starter app.
Link to Youtube Video
(visible only when JS is disabled)
Start building with Gemini 2.5 Pro
You can build with Gemini 2.5 Pro with the Gemini API in
Google AI Studio
, and enterprise customers can use
Vertex AI
.
For developers already using Gemini 2.5 Pro, this new version will not only improve coding performance but will also address key developer feedback including reducing errors in function calling and improving function calling trigger rates. The previous iteration (03-25) now points to the most recent version (05-06), so no action is required to use the improved model, and it continues to be available at the same
price
. We have also
updated the model card
with the new version of 2.5 Pro .
We can’t wait to see the amazing apps you build!

data.title: Show HN: Plexe – ML Models from a Prompt
data.author: vaibhavdubey97
data.article_summary: Plexe是一款通过自然语言描述来构建机器学习模型的工具。用户只需用 plain English 描述所需模型，Plexe 就能通过多智能体架构自动构建并训练模型。它支持多种LLM（大型语言模型）提供商，如OpenAI、Anthropic等，并可通过Ray进行分布式训练以加速模型生成。Plexe还具备自动数据生成和 schema 推断功能，简化了数据准备过程。安装通过 `pip install plexe` 完成，并支持多种安装选项以适应不同需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Plexe项目的优缺点及其应用扩展潜力

不同观点：
• Stiopa：赞赏工作的同时，建议在模型生成过程中增加用户交互，让用户在每一步前确认或修改计划，以提高灵活性。同时，对复杂模型或高级用户的使用场景表示关注。
• Thefourthchime：认为项目创意有趣，但对项目如何解决比大模型本身更独特的问题表示 unclear，希望看到更多这方面的解释。
• Oras：对多方案尝试表示赞同，并关注模型是否能根据数据自行决定创建或微调ML模型，以及是否能检测训练数据的问题。
• Marinr1：表达了对自动化实验和模型训练的兴趣，特别是在GCP环境下的应用，并建议扩展到EDA、模型选择、解释和特征工程等领域。
• Dweinus：虽然认可项目在工作流中的时间节省潜力，但基于2018年autoML的经验，认为项目无法完全自动化ML生命周期，指出数据质量评估和特征设计等难点。
• Fzysingularity：询问项目相比传统建模方法的优势，并建议通过数据集优化提示词以提高性能。
• Gitroom：赞赏项目对传统ML的重视，认为这有助于不失去ML基础。
• Vessenes：对代理组合方法的实用性表示兴趣，询问开发者对smolagent的评价。
• Drlobster：希望项目能成为scikit-learn兼容管道的一部分。
• MarcoDewey：赞赏项目关注传统ML，而非仅限于LLM。

plexe ✨
Build machine learning models using natural language.
Quickstart
|
Features
|
Installation

Documentation
plexe
lets you create machine learning models by describing them in plain language. Simply explain what you want,
and the AI-powered system builds a fully functional model through an automated agentic approach. Also available as a
managed cloud service
.
demo.mp4

Installation
pip install plexe
Using plexe
You can use plexe as a Python library to build and train machine learning models:

(

=

43906346.article_summary: Plexe是一款通过自然语言描述来构建机器学习模型的工具。用户只需用 plain English 描述所需模型，Plexe 就能通过多智能体架构自动构建并训练模型。它支持多种LLM（大型语言模型）提供商，如OpenAI、Anthropic等，并可通过Ray进行分布式训练以加速模型生成。Plexe还具备自动数据生成和 schema 推断功能，简化了数据准备过程。安装通过 `pip install plexe` 完成，并支持多种安装选项以适应不同需求。

data.title: Curl: We still have not seen a valid security report done with AI help
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: Daniel Stenberg, CEO of curl, 表达了对HackerOne平台上大量低质量AI生成的安全报告的不满。他宣布，将要求每个提交报告的人说明是否使用了AI生成报告，并对被认为是AI粗制滥造的报告提交者立即封禁。Stenberg提到，他们尚未看到任何有效的AI辅助安全报告，且这种现象已接近DDoS攻击的程度。他考虑过通过要求提交者支付保证金来提高报告质量，并对AI生成垃圾报告进行过滤。其他用户也提出了类似的担忧和建议，如建立全球黑名单或白名单，以及利用GPT管道处理报告等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（如ChatGPT）在漏洞报告中的使用及其引发的问题

不同观点：
• **danielvf**：认为AI生成的垃圾报告（AI slop）浪费时间，目前为止没有见到任何有效的LLM报告。使用LLM的人往往无法区分有效报告和无意义内容，二次提交的报告甚至更糟。虽然未来可能会有好的AI安全工具，但当前的使用情况令人担忧。
  
• **bogwog**：指出使用AI生成大量无效报告可能是故意为之，目的是通过DDOS方式掩盖真实漏洞报告。这种行为可能是为了获取认可或扰乱项目。

• **vessenes**：建议引入信誉系统，通过AML/KYC验证身份，给予准确报告者更多信誉值，以此提高报告质量。同时认为AI正在改变经济模式，但当前主要是劣化情况（"enshittifying"）。

• **kazinator**：提议对报告者收取可退还的押金，以减少无效报告。如果报告是真实或诚实的错误，押金退还；如果是无意义的报告，押金不退还，以此筛选掉低质量报告。

• **parliament32**：认同报告多为AI生成的幻觉内容，不需查看具体报告即可预见其无效性。

• **rdtsc**：提到报告者公开表示正在寻找工作，暗示其使用AI生成垃圾报告以获取关注。

• **prettyblocks**：质疑如果有人使用AI找到有效安全问题并报告，如何区分AI是否参与其中。

• **uludag**：指出LLM常生成完全虚构的内容，特别是当用户要求其寻找安全漏洞时，存在对齐问题（alignment problem）。

• **jacksnipe**：对频繁引用AI（如ChatGPT）的人感到沮丧，认为如果他们不理解AI的输出，就不应引用。

• **meindnoch**：建议在提交安全报告前，报告者需支付小额押金，若报告为AI slop则押金归审查者所有。

• **ianbutler**：提供反例，指出其团队通过调优的系统找到有效漏洞，并强调区分噪音与有效报告的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成报告的有效性及其对漏洞报告系统的影响。
• 多个建议（如押金制度、信誉系统）被提出以应对无效报告问题。
• 对使用AI工具的伦理及实际效果存在不同看法，部分人认为当前工具误用严重，而部分人认为调优的AI工具可以产生实际效果。

data.title: Is Planet Nine Alone in the Outer System?
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了假设存在的第九行星及其在太阳系外围的探索潜力。作者引用Robert Browning的名言，引出人类探索太空边界的渴望，并提到目前对太阳引力透镜距离（约550 AU）的探索。尽管这一目标超出当前技术能力，但JPL的团队正在进行相关任务设计。文章指出，寻找如第九行星这样的新目标可能激发更多探索兴趣，尤其是如果它类似于在其他星系中发现的超级地球或迷你海王星。

研究显示，许多恒星系统存在超级地球，这支持了第九行星存在的可能性。其质量预计为地球的10倍以上，半长轴约700 AU。尽管光学调查未能发现，但通过比较IRAS和AKARI卫星23年间的数据，研究团队尝试寻找可能的红外源，以确认第九行星的存在。文章强调，尽管技术挑战大，但发现新行星将极大推动太空探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳系外围异常轨道的原因以及是否存在未发现的行星（如第九行星或其它大质量天体）。

不同观点：
• **adrian_b** 认为，许多跨海王星天体的怪异轨道并不能证明当前存在一个巨大的未知行星。他引用2024年发表的论文，提出可能是过去有恒星靠近太阳系，扰动了这些轨道。这种解释比未发现的巨大行星更为合理。

• **Qem** 提到Brown的观点，认为目前观察到的异常轨道并非由假设的第九行星引起，因为该行星的轨道倾角过大，无法产生观察到的效果。同时，Qem还引入了Lykawka和Mukai的独立假设，认为可能存在另一个未被发现的大质量天体，与Batygin和Brown的假设不同。

• **yellowapple** 对冥王星从行星降级表示不满，并幽默地提到不能再将假设中的跨冥王星行星称为“X行星”。

• **soufron** 引用了“Earth in Upheaval”的概念，质疑那颗经过的恒星的时间线。

• **xhrpost** 对DECam相机能否用于后续观测进行了技术性讨论，计算了相机的分辨率和在500AU距离下的观测效果。

补充讨论：
• **ArthurStacks** 和 **WalterBright** 以幽默的方式表达了对该话题的疲惫和调侃，提到过去的讨论和流行文化中的相关情节。

• **RajT88** 和 **eth0up** 以幽默的方式猜测未知天体的外观，分别提到“八号球”和“小黑洞”。

• **cratermoon** 提到过去认为冥王星是最大的跨海王星天体，质疑现在对第九行星的讨论。

• **Hobadee** 坚决认为第九行星就是冥王星，表现出对冥王星行星地位的强烈支持。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于太阳系外围异常轨道的成因，是由于过去有恒星靠近还是因为存在未发现的行星。不同的研究假设和解释形成了对立观点。

43907586.article_content:
Is Planet Nine Alone in the Outer System?
by
Paul Gilster
|
May 6, 2025
|
Outer Solar System
|
2 comments
It was Robert Browning who said “Ah, but a man’s reach should exceed his grasp, or what’s a heaven for?” A rousing thought, but we don’t always know where we should reach. In terms of space exploration, a distant but feasible target is the solar gravitational lens distance beginning around 550 AU. So far the SGL definitely exceeds our grasp, but solid work in mission design by Slava Turyshev and team is ongoing at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Targets need to tantalize, and maybe a target that we hadn’t previously considered is now emerging. Planet Nine, the hypothesized world that may lurk somewhere in our Solar System’s outer reaches, would be such an extraordinary discovery that it would tempt future mission designers in the same way.
This is interesting because right now our deep space targets need to be well defined. I love the idea of
Interstellar Probe
, the craft designed at JHU/APL, but it’s hard to excite the public with the idea of looking back at the heliosphere from the outside (although the science return would be fabulous). Pluto was hard enough to sell to the powers that be, but Allen Stern and team got the job done because they had a whole world that had never been seen up close. Will Planet Nine, if found, turn out to be the destination that some budget-strapped team finds a way to explore?
We have a lot to learn about planetary demographics given that our planet-finding technologies work best for larger worlds closer in to their stars. But a recent microlensing study suggests that as many as one out of every three stars in our galaxy should host a super-Earth in a Jupiter-like orbit (citation below). Microlensing is helpful because it can reveal planets at large distances from their parent stars. Super-Earths appear to be abundant. If it exists, Planet Nine isn’t in a Jovian orbit, but it’s probably smaller than Neptune.
In so many ways this planet makes sense. We’ve found planets like it in innumerable stellar systems. We also know that mechanisms of gravitational slingshotting can push a planet either out of its system entirely or into an entirely new orbit, explaining our prior lack of detection. We’re talking about a planet on the order of a super-Earth or a mini-Neptune, the former larger than our planet but still rocky, the latter smaller than Neptune but gaseous.
Image:
An illustration shows what Planet Nine might look like orbiting far from our Sun. We have found many such worlds around other stars, but finding one in our own backyard is taking time because of its distance and an orbit that is probably well off the ecliptic. Assuming a planet is there at all. Image credit: NASA/Caltech.
The evidence in the orbits of a number of outer system objects points to something perturbing their paths, and seems to implicate something big. Now we have, after years of evidence gathering and debate, at least a possible candidate for this world. In process at
Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia (PASA)
, although not yet published, the paper digs deep into data from the Infrared Astronomical Satellite as well as AKARI, a Japanese satellite somewhat more sensitive than IRAS and launched in 2006.
The distant Sedna and other similar bodies with unusual orbital characteristics tell us that something has to account for their high eccentricity and inclination, while a number of Kuiper Belt objects seem to be similarly affected, as shown in the orientation of their orbits (described through what is known as the
argument of perihelion
). Computations thus far indicate mass on the order of something equal to or greater than 10 Earth masses, with a semi-major axis of about 700 AU.
Image:
The six most distant known objects in the solar system with orbits exclusively beyond Neptune (magenta) all mysteriously line up in a single direction. Moreover, when viewed in 3-D, the orbits of all these icy little objects are tilted in the same direction, away from the plane of the solar system. PL-Caltech/R. Hurt.
A huge amount of work has gone into this analysis, all ably summarized in the paper, which comes from Terry Long Phan (National Tsing Hua University, Taiwan) and colleagues. Optical surveys have heretofore failed to find this object, but 700 AU is fully 23 times the distance of Neptune from the Sun, far enough out that visible wavelengths need to give way to infrared to find it.
Phan’s team looked for candidate objects in the range of 500 to 700 AU using the two far-infrared surveys mentioned above, which are both all-sky in range but separated by 23 years, making for useful comparisons. The idea was to find an object that moved from an IRAS position to an AKARI position after those 23 years. 43907586.article_summary:
文章探讨了假设存在的第九行星及其在太阳系外围的探索潜力。作者引用Robert Browning的名言，引出人类探索太空边界的渴望，并提到目前对太阳引力透镜距离（约550 AU）的探索。尽管这一目标超出当前技术能力，但JPL的团队正在进行相关任务设计。文章指出，寻找如第九行星这样的新目标可能激发更多探索兴趣，尤其是如果它类似于在其他星系中发现的超级地球或迷你海王星。

研究显示，许多恒星系统存在超级地球，这支持了第九行星存在的可能性。其质量预计为地球的10倍以上，半长轴约700 AU。尽管光学调查未能发现，但通过比较IRAS和AKARI卫星23年间的数据，研究团队尝试寻找可能的红外源，以确认第九行星的存在。文章强调，尽管技术挑战大，但发现新行星将极大推动太空探索。

data.title: Show HN: Reverse Pac-Man
data.author: Eagle64
data.article_summary:
"Reverse Pac-Man"是一款与经典《吃豆人》玩法相反的游戏。玩家控制幽灵去捕捉Pac-Man，而非传统中Pac-Man吃豆并躲避幽灵。具体操作如下：  
- 红色幽灵（Ghost 1）：使用WASD或ZQSD键控制移动。  
- 青色幽灵（Ghost 2）：使用方向键控制移动。  

游戏通过反转角色控制，带来新的挑战和乐趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一款类似于Pac-Man的反向操作游戏的反馈和建议

不同观点：
• [操作改进建议] tantalor认为游戏在交叉路口改变方向的机制过于严格，建议允许玩家提前按住按键改变方向，以增加操作的宽容度，而不是在狭窄的时间窗口内检测按键。
• [游戏体验正面评价] KennedyHere对游戏表示了喜爱，但提到游戏标题让他预期引导Pac-Man把点放回原位，这与实际玩法不符。
• [双人控制创新] amadeuspagel赞赏游戏中使用不同按键控制两个角色的创新设计，建议通过颜色区分说明文本以提高可视化。
• [游戏创意评价] pmontra认为这种游戏创意早就该出现，表达了对游戏设计的赞赏。
• [类似游戏对比] narcindin提到一个十年前玩过的类似游戏（swap box turbo），并提供了链接，指出该游戏也采用双人控制机制。
• [游戏推荐] bentcorner推荐了另一款采用双人控制机制的游戏《Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons》，并提供了Steam链接。
• [计分机制疑问] adamiscool8对计分机制表示疑问，不确定是否应该倒计时，还是通过吃掉最多点数获得高分。
• [操作限制批评] kazinator提到幽灵在遇到交叉路口之前不会响应按键，不能立即反方向移动，认为这虽然可能是故意设计的，但仍然让人感到烦恼。
• [控制器支持建议] xnx建议增加双摇杆控制器支持，并提供了相关技术文档链接。
• [技术问题] mtVessel和progforlyfe都遇到了技术问题，前者在Firefox浏览器上遇到安全连接失败错误，后者则完全无法加载游戏。
• [NPC和游戏设计建议] nprateem提到喜欢给NPC赋予背景故事并使其可玩的游戏设计。
• [游戏AI行为观察] roskelld询问是否会加入能量药丸让Pac-Man有反击机会，并观察到Pac-Man在开局时经常无目的地在上左区域绕圈。

补充讨论：
• 玩家对游戏的操作机制、双人控制设计以及计分机制等方面提出了改进建议和疑问。
• 一些玩家分享了类似游戏的经验，并提供了相关链接，丰富了讨论内容。
• 技术问题（如浏览器兼容性和游戏加载问题）也是讨论的一个重要方面。
• 总体来看，玩家对游戏的创新设计表示赞赏，但对其操作限制和计分机制存在一定争议。

data.title: DoomArena: A Framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为DoomArena的框架，用于测试AI代理面对不断演变的安全威胁。该框架基于三个原则：可插拔设计，易于集成到实际代理框架中；可配置，支持详细的威胁建模；模块化，攻击开发与环境细节解耦，允许跨多个环境应用相同攻击。DoomArena具有适应新威胁模型和环境、结合多种攻击进行全面安全测试、分析漏洞与性能权衡等优势。实验显示，当前最先进的（SOTA）网络和工具调用代理对不同威胁模型的脆弱性各异，基于强大SOTA LLM的防御效果更佳。DoomArena代码已开源。

View PDF
Abstract:
We present DoomArena, a security evaluation framework for AI agents. DoomArena is designed on three principles: 1) It is a plug-in framework and integrates easily into realistic agentic frameworks like BrowserGym (for web agents) and $\tau$-bench (for tool calling agents); 2) It is configurable and allows for detailed threat modeling, allowing configuration of specific components of the agentic framework being attackable, and specifying targets for the attacker; and 3) It is modular and decouples the development of attacks from details of the environment in which the agent is deployed, allowing for the same attacks to be applied across multiple environments. We illustrate several advantages of our framework, including the ability to adapt to new threat models and environments easily, the ability to easily combine several previously published attacks to enable comprehensive and fine-grained security testing, and the ability to analyze trade-offs between various vulnerabilities and performance. We apply DoomArena to state-of-the-art (SOTA) web and tool-calling agents and find a number of surprising results: 1) SOTA agents have varying levels of vulnerability to different threat models (malicious user vs malicious environment), and there is no Pareto dominant agent across all threat models; 2) When multiple attacks are applied to an agent, they often combine constructively; 3) Guardrail model-based defenses seem to fail, while defenses based on powerful SOTA LLMs work better. DoomArena is available at

.

data.title: Free with In-App Purchase is a sham
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文批评了苹果App Store中“免费+内购”应用程序的误导性标签，指出其定义模糊，容易让消费者混淆。作者认为，苹果所谓的“免费”仅指下载时无需付费，但并未清楚说明使用应用时可能需要的付费内容，导致不同应用的内购范围和限制差异巨大。一些应用甚至在下载后无法使用，除非用户先支付内购费用，而苹果对这种“诱导转换”策略并无明显反对。作者举例说明某款排名靠前的应用存在误导性定价和不透明的取消订阅指引，批评苹果的审核团队未能有效保护消费者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应用商店中的“免费+内购”模式及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [hedora的观点] 认为文章中提到的问题源于App Store的筛选不力，而不是“免费+内购”模式本身。他提到自己使用一些免费但包含内购的应用程序，并没有遇到问题。
• [AStoneThrow的观点] 基于Google Play商店的体验，指出“免费+内购”模式在实际使用中可能会变得混乱，尤其是在多个设备和账户之间切换时，容易导致用户对已购买内容的混淆。他还提到，对于不熟悉的应用，用户希望先试用再决定是否购买，而“免费+内购”模式在这种情况下更为合适。同时，他也承认有些开发者可能故意让用户混淆，从而让用户重复付费。
• [dlachausse的观点] 认为“免费+内购”模式利用了消费者的心理，他们更倾向于选择免费的应用，并逐步被引导进行内购消费。虽然一次性付费可能对用户更有利，但这种模式难以与“免费”应用竞争。

补充讨论：
• 一些应用提供两种版本，一个是直接付费的“高级版”，另一个是免费但包含内购的“试用版”，这种双重列表可能会导致用户混淆，尤其是在多个设备和账户之间切换时。
• AStoneThrow提到，某些应用通过辅助应用（如“Supporter”应用）来解锁主应用的高级功能，这种做法虽然解决了某些问题，但也增加了用户的困惑。
• dlachausse指出，消费者往往被“免费”标签吸引，即使最终可能在内购上花费更多，这种心理倾向使得“免费+内购”模式在市场上更具竞争力。

争议焦点：
• “免费+内购”模式是否是必要的，还是由于应用商店机制不完善导致的。
• 用户在使用“免费+内购”模式时，是否因混淆而导致重复付费，这是否是开发者的有意设计。

43907763.article_content:
Free with In-App Purchase is a sham
May 6 2025
A couple of weeks ago I published a blog post about
App Store Curation
. At the end I said:
Apple claims that locking down iOS to the App Store is justified in order to protect consumers from danger. Time and again, however, it's painfully obvious that Apple's so-called "curation" of the App Store is terrible, miserable, incompetent, negligent.
By the way, the app I wrote about,
Virus Protection for Phone
, was removed from the App Store shortly thereafter. Perhaps Apple should pay me to do their job for them. How about a bounty for scams? I'll take, say, 30% of their revenue.
In this blog post, I want to discuss a fundamental, intentional design flaw of the App Store that misleads consumers: the category of apps that are labeled as free with In-App Purchase. The App Store shows an explanation of In-App Purchases when you click the Learn More link in the In-App Purchases section of an app's product page; here's a quote from the first paragraph of Apple's document:
Many of your favorite free and paid apps and games offer in-app purchases, which are optional transactions that change an app's functionality or unlock digital goods, content or services. You can find out if an app offers in-app purchases by visiting its product page in the App Store. Just look for the "In-App Purchases" messages near the Get or Price button.
The problem is that what Apple means here by "free" as opposed to "paid" is simply that you don't have to pay before downloading the app, but Apple's counterintuitive definition tends to obscure what is most important to consumers: how much you have to pay to
use
the app. The range of allowed use can vary drastically among apps that are free with IAP. Some apps can be used forever for free with no apparent limitations, and the IAP merely unlocks bonus content or features. Some can be used for free in "reader" mode, with the ability to open and read documents, while an IAP is required to edit and/or sync documents. Some apps are free to use fully for only a limited time; in other words, they have a time-limited free trial. At the end of the trial, various outcomes are possible. Time-limited trials are especially popular with auto-renewing subscription apps, which start charging you automatically at the end of the trial. And ironically, some so-called "free" apps don't allow any use at all unless you first pay the IAP.
Three years ago,
I highlighted such an app
that was free to download but could not be used in any way without the IAP. In response to the ensuing negative publicity, the developer of the app added a time-limited free trial. Nonetheless, Apple had already approved the app without a free trial, and there's no evidence that Apple or its app review team has any objection to the bait-and-switch tactic. As
Nick Heer wrote at the time:
This is the kind of thing Apple sought to prevent when it launched In-App Purchases as a
feature for paid apps only
. Opening them up to free apps has created different purchasing mechanisms in the App Store and has pushed the industry toward subscription pricing, but it has also enabled scummy behaviour like this.
The app in question is still
in the Mac App Store
, apparently renamed from "Docs Pro for Google Drive" to "Docs for Google Docs and Drive", but still labeled as free with IAP. In fact it's one of the Mac App Store's most financially successful apps, currently ranked #33 top grossing the United States,
according to AppFigures
.
Below is a screenshot of the app's window now on first launch (click to see full size):
You might be shocked to learn that the window is actually
floating
. That is, it floats above and covers every other window on the Mac, even if you switch to a different app. And Apple approved this. You can close the floating window, but that quits the app.
By default, the lifetime $39.99 license is selected. It's labeled "Best choice - no subscription". The 3 day free trial is available only if you select the $19.99 yearly subscription option. The subtitle of the subscription option says, "Only $5.00/month", the math of which is
way
off and would add up to $60 per year if accurate. I don't know how that window got approved by Apple.
To get the free trial, I selected the subscription option.
The instructions for canceling the trial are vague, "in your account". This may be unhelpful or even confusing for novice App Store users, the very people most in need of Apple's protection. Adding to the potential confusion, as soon as you press OK, a new window opens asking you to Sign in to Google with your Google account. (I'll present evidence of customer confusion later in this blog post, in the form of App Store user reviews.)
Fortunately, I did receive a subscription confirmation email from Apple that included a link to my Apple Account subscriptions management page and confirmed the terms of the subscription: "To avoid being charged, you must cancel at least a day before each billing date."

data.title: Instant (YC S22) Is Hiring a Founding TypeScript Engineer
data.author: stopachka
data.article_summary: Instant 是一个结合了 Firebase 和 Supabase 优点的实时数据库，支持关系同步。其团队正在寻找一位创始 TypeScript 工程师，要求对类型设计有极致追求，能够提升开发者体验，并帮助构建类似 Figma 或 Notion 的同步引擎。团队希望优化类型的智能提示和性能，例如通过自动补全和类型安全改善查询体验，并提升 CLI 和 Dashboard 的用户界面，使其更直观和高效。此外，团队还计划改进迁移支持、沙盒功能和数据浏览器，以打造更完善的开发者工具。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43897138.article_content:
instant
instant
Founding Typescript Engineer
Instant is a real-time database you can use on the frontend. We give you the best of both Firebase and Supabase, a sync-engine with support for relations. This is the kind of tech that companies like Figma, Notion, and Linear build internally to power their products (
Try out the demo
)
We're looking for a founding Typescript Engineer to join our team of 4 in San Francisco. If you:
Are obsessive about type ergonomics (even with how types show up in intellisense)
Enjoy crafting UIs that people use for hours
Want to build a sync engine to enable the next Figma or Notion
Then we want to talk to you! So, why those three points? Let us explain:
1
.
You are obsessive about type ergonomics
One of the benefits about using typescript in a library is the developer experience you can offer your users. Types can do so much more than just catch typos. Types are a tool. They give you autocomplete and good feedback; shown in the right moment they can make someone's day. We don't just want to build a great database. We want people to enjoy using it.
Instant is
typed
. It took some serious
type fu
, but the upshot is the users get autocomplete and typesafety as a result. And right now types are a first cut. Here's some of what's ahead:
Type where clauses
Imagine you are building a goodreads alternative. You want to write a query like:
Give me profiles that have "Count of Monte Cristo" in their bookshelves
. This is how it would look in Instant:
{
profiles
:
{
$
:
{
where
:
{
"bookshelves.books.title"
:
"Count of Monte Cristo"
}
}
,
}
}
;
And with it you'd get those profiles. But
bookshelves.books.title
is typed too broadly: any string is allowed. This means users could have typos, or forget which relationships exist on
profiles
.
Well, we already have access to the schema. We
could
type the where clause. This way, when a user starts writing "booksh", we could autocomplete with all the relationships that live on
profiles
!
This is tricky (there's
a lot
you can do in a query), but it would be a huge benefit to users.
Improve intellisense
Or speaking of
schemas
: this is what you'll see in Typescript when you hover over one:
const
schema
:
InstantSchemaDef
<
EntitiesWithLinks
<
{
profiles
:
EntityDef
<
{
name
:
DataAttrDef
<
string
,
true
>
;
}
,
{
}
,
void
>
;
bookshelves
:
EntityDef
<
{
title
:
DataAttrDef
<
string
,
true
>
;
}
,
{
}
,
void
>
;
}
,
{
...
;
}
>
,
LinksDef
<
...
>
,
RoomsDef
>
Now, complex types can look notoriously daunting in intellisense. Some of the complexity is unavoidable, but there's a
lot
that can be done to improve it. For example, is it really necessary that the hover includes
EntitiesWithLinks
,
EntityDef
,
DataAttrDef
?
Some may think it's not worth fretting over intellisense output. But you know this differentiates the best libraries. Great types reap great benefits.
Performance, utility types...
And the list goes on. We want to add more tests for type outputs (one project we're considering is to write a library that tests
intellisense
output). We want to write benchmarks to see how types perform in larger codebases. We want to improve how you define schemas and how you write transactions. We want to add more utility types, so users can build their own libraries on top of Instant.
2
.
You enjoy crafting UIs that people use for hours
Today Instant ships with a
CLI tool
and a
Dashboard
.
Since Instant is a core part of our user's infra, they end up spending hours every day interacting with it. The onus is on us to make their experience as delightful as possible. UIs make a real difference here. People may not consciously notice it, but every detail adds up. There's a lot of work to do:
Migrations in the CLI
Right now, you can push your schema with the
CLI
, but we don't support any destructive actions. You can add a column, but you can't delete it (You can do this manually). We held off on destructive actions in the CLI, because we wanted to make the right kind of UX: something that feels natural, but doesn't let you shoot yourself in the foot. Can you help design it and implement it? Maybe it's time we add migrations, or take inspiration from terraform.
Better Sandbox
In the dashboard, we have a
sandbox
that lets you run queries and transactions:
You can dry-run transactions, make queries, and see how your permissions work. Users live in this tool for hours. But there's a lot missing here. For example, could you save snippets, or have a history of the changes you've made to your sandbox?
Better Explorer
Or take a look at the
Explorer
. It lets you visually query and change data. This often replaces custom code users would have needed to write for an admin panel. You can already make queries, create rows, link objects, and upload files:
But this is just the beginning. What else do users use an admin panel for, and how can we just give it to them? We want to make an editing experience on level of Airtable, available to every dev before they even start bui

主要讨论点：Kubernetes配置管理工具的选择与使用

不同观点：
• atmosx认为Kustomize在大规模管理时更易用，但需要前期投入。他提到许多图表作为Helm包分发，因此需要导出为YAML。他建议结合ArgoCD使用Kustomize，但在需要动态替换变量时可能需要使用envsubst。

• arccy表示如果只处理自己的项目，可以避免使用Helm，他推荐使用CUE生成Kubernetes YAML。他提到如果需要类似Helm的体验但使用CUE，可以考虑Timoni。他还指出，处理上游项目时，可能不得不使用Helm或重写它们。

• haiku2077使用ArgoCD处理简单任务，对于复杂任务则编写Python或Go程序生成清单，然后使用kubectl应用。

• b11484提到正在改进一个使用Jsonnet的工具kr8+，用于组合集群配置并应用到组件。

• bithavoc使用Pulumi的原生包进行Kubernetes管理，完全避免YAML，只使用TypeScript类实例。

• dvektor不喜欢将Git仓库作为Helm图表，但同时也认为不使用Helm而手写各种YAML文件更糟糕。

• Nerudite推荐Helmsman工具，提供了一个GitHub链接。

• Vespasian推荐使用fluxcd进行GitOps工作流，并提到其整合了处理秘密信息的soap。

• LarsLarson分享了他们使用Kustomize创建YAML并用ArgoCD进行部署的经验，通过CI和GitOps工作良好。

• natbennett偏好使用ytt进行模板处理，使用kapp进行部署，提供了一个Carvel项目的链接。

• delduca表示支持使用Kustomize。

• johnjungles简单表示支持ArgoCD。

补充讨论：
- 讨论涉及多种工具的比较和选择，如Kustomize、Helm、CUE、Pulumi、ArgoCD、fluxcd、ytt、kapp等。
- 不同工具的优缺点和适用场景被多次提到，例如Helm在处理上游项目时的必要性与麻烦，以及Kustomize在动态配置和管理上的优势。
- 争议焦点在于是否使用Helm及其图表，以及如何有效管理Kubernetes配置以满足不同工作流需求。

data.title: Technical analysis of the Signal clone used by Trump officials
data.author: micahflee
data.article_summary: 本文披露了特朗普政府官员使用的一款非官方Signal克隆应用——TM SGNL，该应用由TeleMessage公司开发，能够自动存档明文消息，甚至包括那些设置为阅后即焚的消息。TM SGNL利用Signal的服务器进行端到端加密通讯，但会将聊天记录存档到其他可能不安全的地方，如Gmail账户。该应用疑似违反了Signal的开源许可证，且未公开提供下载，仅通过企业设备管理服务分发。TeleMessage公司高管多有以色列国防军情报部门的背景，其行为可能涉及违规使用Signal及其他软件的专有许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Signal加密通信系统的安全性及其在政府和特朗普行政部门的应用

不同观点：
• [tomhow] 和 [abhisek] 提到了将Signal等端到端加密消息存档到可能破坏其安全模型的存储系统中的矛盾。abhisek特别质疑这种做法是否违背了使用Signal的初衷，即为了安全和隐私。
• [cycomanic] 和 [mdhb] 提到了Telemessage应用的漏洞以及其与外国情报机构的关系。cycomanic指出Telemessage已经被黑客攻击，而mdhb则关注该应用由前以色列情报官员控制，暗示可能存在安全隐患。
• [ComputerGuru] 和 [ThinkBeat] 讨论了政府官员使用Signal的合法性以及是否存在由美国军方或NSA开发的专用安全通信工具。ComputerGuru特别质疑Telemessage是否得到了官方批准，而ThinkBeat则推测是否存在一个结合硬件和软件的专用通信系统。
• [egberts1] 和 [throw7] 关心TM SGNL（Telemessage的Signal克隆版）是否被Signal官方允许连接到Signal网络，以及其安全性是否会因此受损。throw7特别质疑Signal是否允许非官方版本的应用连接到其网络。
• [mmooss] 和 [lrvick] 深入讨论了使用非官方客户端（如TM SGNL）可能导致的安全漏洞，尤其是消息存档和删除策略的不一致。mmooss担心用户使用非官方客户端会破坏Signal的安全保证，而lrvick提出了一种技术方案来实现消息存档的同时保持端到端加密。

补充讨论：
• [gbraad] 指出，由于没有对实际二进制文件进行技术分析，因此无法确定应用是否被修改。这种分析依赖于文档和分配过程。
• [be_erik] 认为，虽然不希望政府官员使用Signal，但Signal本身是一个优秀的安全通信工具。
• [jimmydoe] 讽刺地评论了特朗普行政部门遵循法律存档聊天记录的做法，并批评了Telemessage的技术 incompetence。
• [ThinkBeat] 提到政府官员使用“工作”和“私人”手机的做法，工作手机通常经过加固并使用安全的政府VPN系统。

争议焦点：
• 是否应将端到端加密的消息存档，特别是当存档过程可能破坏其加密安全性时。
• Telemessage等第三方应用是否得到了适当的批准和审查，尤其是考虑到其潜在的安全隐患和与外国情报机构的关系。
• Signal是否应对非官方客户端进行标识，以确保用户通信的安全性和隐私性。
